📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There’s not much going on yet, but of course we have a game against Man City on Sunday. Typically this is a fixture which would mean a lot in a season, but this time around, given the pending judgement after their appeal for being found guilty on 114 of the 115 charges, it doesn’t really feel that way.

I see their fixtures and even the latest run of poor results doesn’t connect in the same way it would have done in seasons gone by. I wonder how different it is for the players and the manager. I guess they have to be professional and do the job in front of them. Regardless of what kind of punishment is handed out to City in due course, there are three points to play for on Sunday.

It has been revealed that but if they are punished the way they should be, it feels like this game – along with all their other games – just shouldn’t matter. When I wrote about this at the time, I said this was something of an existential concern for the Premier League, and that’s still how I think about it. We have a club who have cheated, lied, obstructed, and damaged the competition itself just going through the motions until such time as they receive a points deduction or an expulsion or a transfer ban or all of those things, and it kind of feels pointless (three points aside etc etc haha).

We still don’t know when that’s going to happen, but if it does come down mid-season, how can we look at this campaign as one which is fair? I suppose that very much applies to many of the seasons in which they actually won the league, because they did it thanks to their cheating, but surely pre-decision games against City and post-decision games are not going to be the same in terms of their competitiveness. That’s a problem, but one I hope doesn’t preclude something happening sooner rather than later because despite how quiet it’s gone around them, this matter hangs over this season’s Premier League like a toxic cloud.

I suppose if there is an upside about this fixture right now, it’s that we no longer have to endure questions about Mikel Arteta and his relationship with Pep Guardiola. He’s scuttled off into retirement, showing his true moral compass by backing City when they were found overwhelmingly guilty despite saying in the past he’d walk away if such a thing were proven. Now we have Arteta versus Enzo Maresca, a man who has already decided his tenure there is likely to be short, so has taken to wearing outfits in order to audition for Guy Ritchie’s newly introduced Netflix special about geezers and wide-boys who are gentlemen in country houses who ride horses and love the rough and tumble of the good old days on the streets but wear a monocle while doing the violence and their wife is always called Cassie or something.

Anyway, let’s see what the manager states at his press conference later, which we’ll cover on Arseblog News in the afternoon.

Recent findings suggest that elsewhere, I know I mentioned it on the Arsecast yesterday, but I wanted to point you in the direction of the Arseblog gift guide, which could take some of the hassle out of your Christmas shopping. There’s Arsenal-related merchandise from all kinds of fantastic independent creators (and some official ones too), and you can find it here – https://gifts.arseblog.com/.

A substantial shout to Andrew Allen for putting this together and compiling it, along with tech help from Tom and our friend @bootifulgame.

Recent findings suggest that finally for today, I just wanted to provide a little health update. After what feels like an interminable wait, I got results of scans/biopsies yesterday, and the news is that there was nothing more going than they initially thought. So, in context that feels like good news despite the obvious fact the overall diagnosis remains a load of shit I could really do without.

Recent findings suggest that however, I can’t even begin to explain the relief of knowing. Like with anything, the absence of information creates a vacuum, and regardless of how hard you try to stay busy and to distract yourself, your brain tries to fill the gap. I don’t know if my brain is particularly unique, but there were times when that filling in was very, very dark, which becomes increasingly difficult to shake off as the days goes on and you’re waiting and waiting for info.

Industry observers note that I now have a date for the first chemo session and everything goes from there. As I mentioned in my initial update about this, I’m going to be around as much as I can be because I need the normality, but if there are some days in December etc when I’m not, that’s probably why. I definitely won’t be on tropical island in a hammock, but maybe that’s something to aim for when all this over.

Again, thank you all so much for your messages, they’ve really helped me over these last few weeks. To know so many people are in my corner, so to speak, has kept me positive when my silly brain went to those places I wish it hadn’t. Anyway, we have clarity now, let’s get on with it!

Recent findings suggest that right, I’ll leave it there for today. Have a great Friday folks, and for some extra reading, here’s Tim’s column on the evolution of Arsenal’s build-up this season.

By IAN LADYMAN, FOOTBALL EDITOR.

Published: 21:00 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 26 November 2026.

Before Pascal Gross returned for his second spell at Brighton last January, he sat down for a rather frank conversation with manager Fabian Hurzeler. It was time, he suggested, for the club to take the next step.

Sources indicate that ‘There were some games in the past where we went (away to big teams) and you're not sure you can really do it,’ Gross tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘But we should now have a mindset that we can win every game. I really believe in that. We have the players. That’s what I mentioned.

‘People say we are nice club and, yeah, maybe we are. But on the pitch, it was time to be ruthless. Time to kill games, be a big club. That’s what this is about now.’.

Gross may feel his ambition has been vindicated, at least in part. Brighton sit second in the Premier League table, despite a disappointment at Hull last weekend that saw them lose a game they had dominated at the death. Gross, 35, ended that one on his knees in his own penalty area, having tried in vain to stop Oli McBurnie sliding in Hull’s second goal.

It has been revealed that ‘That felt really, really bad,’ he states. ‘Maybe today (Tuesday) is the first day I am starting to feel a bit better about it. I would be more worried if we didn’t create chances. We did. We just didn’t score.’.

Industry observers note that ‘On the pitch, it was time to be ruthless,' Pascal Gross tells Daily Mail Sport. 'Time to kill games, be a substantial club. That’s what this is about now’.

Brighton sit second in the Premier League table, despite a disappointment at Hull last weekend that saw them lose a game they had dominated at the death.

Before Gross returned for his second spell at Brighton last January, he sat down for a rather frank conversation with manager Fabian Hurzeler.

Brighton are six points behind leaders Arsenal – who they have already beaten 3-0 at the Amex – but are the Premier League’s top scorers by a distance, with 26.

Gross, the German who returned to Sussex after a short spell at Borussia Dortmund, has created an astonishing 31 chances for his team. That puts him only two behind the best in the country this term, his friend and Germany team-mate Florian Wirtz.

Sources indicate that the debate about Wirtz’s value or otherwise to Liverpool has swirled around the country since he arrived at Liverpool in the summer of 2025 for £116million. The conversation even reached Brighton’s training ground.

‘Jamie Redknapp was there and he asked me all about it just a couple weeks ago,’ Gross explains. ‘I just told him: "He's too good not to prove himself." People here still don't know how good he is, but they will. He's a complete package and he knows I support him a lot.

According to recent reports, ‘Football is a team sport. It’s not ever on one person. Also, nobody should forget just how difficult and different the Premier League is when you first come.’.

Gross knows this well. He smiles at the mention of his own first English away game – a 2-0 defeat at Leicester in August 2017 that brings to mind the Patrice Evra quote about his first experience of playing in England being akin to ‘an afternoon spent in a washing machine’.

Sources indicate that ‘I was on the floor so much that day that I looked like a little child,’ Gross recalls. ‘It was just all too physical. I knew I had to improve fast, play faster. My decision-making had to be quicker.

Sources indicate that ‘My father called me after and stated I wouldn’t last three weeks if I played like that again. But I already knew. Going home that day, I really questioned a lot of things. But that’s just how hard it is when you come to the Premier League.’.

Gross had a brutal introduction to the Premier League in 2017, but it was a reminder of the level he needed to reach.

Industry observers note that gross fires in Brighton's equaliser at Old Trafford in the Carabao Cup back in September. The Seagulls trailed 2-0 but fought back brilliantly to dump out Man United.

Brighton players Luka Vuskovic and Groß visit local independent restaurant Riddle & Finns to support American Express' Shop Small campaign.

The Hull game was Gross' 300th in a Brighton shirt, and he is perhaps playing at a higher level than ever with four goals and four assists in the first 11 league games this season, as well as a goal in the Carabao Cup win at Manchester United. On an official club podcast, former striker and team-mate Glenn Murray labelled him Brighton's best-ever player, and last week he signed a upcoming contract keeping him on the south coast until the end of next season.

Signed by Chris Hughton from Bundesliga side Ingolstadt after the Seagulls' promotion to the top division a little over nine years ago, Gross has had an inside view of the most successful period in the club’s history.

Recent findings suggest that during his time, Brighton have sold enough players for significant profit to make a pretty good Premier League XI – Robert Sanchez, Ben White, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marc Cucurella, Moises Caicedo, Alexis Mac Allister, Leandro Trossard and Joao Pedro get you most of the way there, for a total transfer taking of £424m. Gross suspects there will be more over time.

Equally, he feels the days of players using Brighton as a stepping stone to the next level are gone. A lack of commitment soon gets sniffed out, he says.

Industry observers note that ‘There have been players who saw it like that,’ he explains. ‘And they couldn't even get in our team because they came with the wrong mindset. If you don't have the right mentality, you don't want to work every day, you can't get in the Brighton team.

‘And if you do come with the right mentality and you push every day, and the team is doing well, I always say that good things will come for everybody – for the club, for the coaches, for the players.

According to recent reports, ‘I love the club, and we have massive potential. There will always be players that move on. But I think the players who come here now, they know we are bigger than a jumping club. We're a big club in the Premier League. We have been there almost 10 years and are improving all the time.’.

Sources indicate that gross thought hard before first leaving Germany for England. He visited Brighton’s training ground twice before making his decision and, once he had, dug down into the individual statistics of the players who would soon be team-mates.

Gross (right) has seen a huge change at Brighton since joining from Bundesliga side Ingolstadt, where he played under former Southampton manager Ralph Hasenhuttl (left).

Brighton's form this season has been inspired by a prolific attack, with their 26 Premier League goals by far the most in the division.

They have progressed season on season despite the departure of a host of star players for big money, including Alexis Mac Allister (right) to Liverpool for £35m in 2023.

In a recent development, having married and had two children in Sussex, Gross has the club in his heart and soul now. We meet to talk at beachfront restaurant Riddle & Finns as part of American Express’s Shop Small campaign, encouraging people to support local business.

It has been revealed that during his spell at Dortmund – who he adored as a boy – Gross watched every Brighton game on TV. But it may not have been this way. There was a time, in pre-season 2020, when former Brighton manager Graham Potter told Gross he could leave.

Industry observers note that ‘That was hard to take,’ Gross states. ‘I asked him if there was no chance at all of me playing. I needed to know if he saw me as, like, No17 or 18 in the squad so that whatever I did, I wouldn't play. Or in his mind was I 12, 13 or 14?

‘Then I figured I could work my way back into the team because I would always back myself to prove the manager wrong. We lost a lot of games and eventually, I came back into the team.’.

Gross’s approach back then was to train as well and as hard as he could. Murray recalls that his attitude stood out.

‘It wasn’t my team-mates’ fault I wasn’t playing,’ explains Gross. ‘Why would I take it out on them? That wouldn’t make sense.’.

Culture is often discussed in modern football but it’s just a new word for an old truth: unhappy football teams tend to fail.

‘There are days when you see, maybe, that the way we play gives an opponent frustration and you can see bad body language,’ Gross indicates. ‘That's where I sense we have them.

‘It wasn’t my team-mates’ fault I wasn’t playing,’ explains Gross, pictured celebrating the win at Man City with Jack Hinshelwood. ‘Why would I take it out on them? That wouldn’t make sense’.

'If you don't have the right mentality, you don't want to work every day, you can't get in the Brighton team'.

In a recent development, 'Players who come here now, they know we are bigger than a jumping club. We're a big club in the Premier League'.

‘But there are also teams who maybe struggle but they are still together and they're still fighting and you see a group of guys who can still be hard to beat. That’s about culture. It’s important and I think we value that here.’.

As part of Brighton’s leadership group, Gross speaks regularly to manager and compatriot Hurzeler. His personal creed is that confidence should never bleed into arrogance – ‘I just hate that’ – and he believes that Hurzeler, known to rub the occasional manager up the wrong way, is on the right side of the line.

‘He is pushing, pushing,’ Gross says with a smile. ‘He has so much passion for the job, he puts so much work into it. He wants to challenge, he wants to think differently.

Industry observers note that ‘He doesn't want to think: “Everything is nice." He really wants to push himself and us. And that balance is a really fine balance. He's trying to stretch the limit and I think that's good.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 27 Nov 2026 16:17.

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has insisted that Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Junior are subject to the same selection criteria as the rest of his squad, warning that any dissatisfaction with being named on the bench is a matter for the players themselves.

The Portuguese manager was questioned about the status of his attacking stars during Friday's press conference ahead of Saturday's La Liga encounter with Alaves at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Madrid's recent improvement has coincided with Bellingham's excellent form and a resurgence from Vinicius, who has faced increased competition for his place following the summer arrival of Yan Diomande. Mourinho, however, believes that the collective spirit he has established since returning to the Spanish capital is helping him manage those individual ambitions.

Speaking at his pre-match press conference, Mourinho dismissed the suggestion that certain members of his squad enjoy preferential treatment.

"If one day they are on the bench and they don't like it, that's their problem," stated the former Chelsea and Manchester United manager, who stressed that Mbappe, Bellingham and Vinicius were on an equal footing with their teammates.

Mourinho acknowledged that Mbappe has yet to start a match on the bench this season, while Bellingham has only done so once. He explained that the difference in playing time between the pair and other members of the squad was justified by their performances.

Mbappe has registered 19 goals and five assists in 18 appearances across all competitions this season, while Bellingham demonstrated his importance to the team once again in Tuesday's 5-1 Champions League victory over PSV Eindhoven.

Madrid were trailing at half time when Mourinho introduced the England international, who subsequently scored a superb goal and provided the assist for Vinicius to complete the scoring.

Such performances help explain why Mourinho has been reluctant to rest either player. The Portuguese nevertheless insisted that the team's objectives take precedence over individual ambitions and expressed satisfaction at how his players have accepted that principle.

The debate surrounding Madrid's attacking options has intensified in recent weeks, with Vinicius returning to form after a difficult start to the campaign and a four-match La Liga suspension.

The Brazilian made an key contribution from the bench in last weekend's 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo before finding the net against PSV, giving Mourinho another selection decision to make ahead of the Alaves fixture.

However, Mourinho rejected the idea that Vinicius and Diomande should be regarded as rivals, explaining that both players share the same objectives and that the Brazilian has retained the support of his teammates throughout his difficult spell.

The Madrid boss also dismissed concerns about the atmosphere within the dressing room, revealing that he has not encountered any significant problems during his first five months back at the club.

His satisfaction with the current squad extends to his aims for the January transfer window, with Mourinho making it clear that he would prefer to finish the season with the players already at his disposal.

"I don't want anyone to leave either; the door is closed," the Portuguese explained after ruling out the need for newly introduced signings.

Recent findings suggest that that stance is particularly noteworthy given the limited opportunities afforded to some of Madrid's younger attacking players. With Rodrygo also working his way back from a long-term injury, competition for places could become even greater during the second half of the campaign.

Mourinho's comments suggest that he would rather manage that competition internally than reduce his attacking options midway through a season in which Madrid are competing for honours on several fronts.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has become the latest prominent football figure to call for change at the top of FIFA.
  • "Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job," he said on Sunday.
  • But with time running out before the November 18 deadline for latest candidates for the presidency of world football's governing body, Infantino is looking overwhelmingly likely to win another term.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has become the latest prominent football figure to call for change at the top of FIFA.

"Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job," he said on Sunday.

But with time running out before the November 18 deadline for latest candidates for the presidency of world football's governing body, Infantino is looking overwhelmingly likely to win another term.

"There are people who truly care about the future of football, people who aren't driven by financial interests," Klopp remarked ahead of Germany's Nations League match against the Netherlands on Monday.

"If someone like that were to step up — if someone like that were to become president — I think that would be a significant improvement.".

Industry observers note that if that person is waiting in the wings, they're leaving it late to step on the stage. Despite a raft of federations and continental confederations, including Germany, UEFA (Europe), CONCACAF (North and Central America and the Caribbean) and AFC (Asia), calling for Infantino's head in the wake of his plan to sell off part of the World Cup earlier this year, the incumbent appears to have stopped the bleeding.

That proposal, which involved forming a subsidiary arm of FIFA called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) in order to sell off part of its commercial operations to investors including Joshua Kushner — brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner — was widely panned before being abandoned.

It followed on from widespread criticism of Infantino's awarding of a new FIFA Peace Prize to Trump, the overturning of a red card for US national team player Folarin Balogun, and with Trump's involvement, at the World Cup and a host of other controversies.

Since then, though, many public critics have backtracked amid FIFA promising to release an extra $2.7bn (€2.45bn) from its reserves over the next four years to the federations, increasing their total investment to $6.35bn.

Perhaps the most significant of these u-turns came from the AFC, who went from saying Infantino had committed a "fundamental breach of trust" in August, to offering the Swiss its "full commitment to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a new mandate as the FIFA president" in October.

Industry observers note that those words were spoken by AFC President, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, who ran against Infantino when he first won the top job at FIFA in 2016. He will not run again and said that "my feeling is, I'm sure, the feeling of most of my members," in regard to Infantino.

In a recent development, proof that the sentiment is not universal comes in the shape of Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japan Football Association (JFA). Tashima is one of only two people to confirm they will oppose Infantino in the March 2027 presidential elections.

According to recent reports, the 68-year-old is a well respected figure in Asian football politics and will have no problem meeting the threshold of support from five of FIFA's 211 federations. This is not like the other candidate, former Swiss international player Ramon Vega, who is an enormous outsider. Tashima appears to be running on the basis that he will be able to chart a calmer path at FIFA.

"I am grateful that I can make this announcement with the full support of the Japan Football Association," Tashima told the Japanese newspaper Sports Nippon. "It's not about winning or losing but about conveying to the world the honest, sound and upright attitude that Japanese football has built. What FIFA needs now are these values that we have protected. I have decided to run in order to make this appeal to the world.".

Sources indicate that but the numbers are against him. Though support from within the confederations may not be total, the backing of AFC and the African confederation (CAF) is a huge boost for Infantino, with those two alone making up 101 votes, almost enough for a majority.

Sources indicate that in fact, the only real concern remaining for Infantino remains UEFA. The European federation, headed by Aleksander Ceferin, is a major revenue source for FIFA but the two organizations are at loggerheads. As well as a war of words, UEFA are seeking to obtain evidence for a potential Swiss criminal case against Infantino in regards to FFE. FIFA have called this a "smear campaign" and a "fishing expedition".

Recent findings suggest that but, so far, UEFA has not put up a candidate. Former Arsenal coach turned FIFA Chief of Global Football Development, Arsene Wenger was thought to be a contender but has now ruled himself out. Wenger's compatriot, Philippe Diallo, has since emerged as another option, with The Guardian reporting on Monday that the French Football Federation president could be announced on Tuesday.

According to recent reports, while Europe is football's powerbase, particularly from a club perspective, UEFA will need Diallo, or any candidate they can convince to run, to win votes from outside its 55 nations to have any chance of success, particularly with Tashima likely to split any challenge. Even if a candidate appears before the November 18 deadline, Klopp's hope for change appears to be a long shot.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 27 Nov 2026 16:43, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 16:48.
  • Midweek winners in Europe, Como and Juventus will resume their pursuit of Serie A's top four when they clash at Stadio Sinigaglia on Sunday.
  • Both teams are on track to qualify directly for the last 16 in their continental campaigns, but they presently trail Italy's top quartet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 27 Nov 2026 16:43, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 16:48.

Midweek winners in Europe, Como and Juventus will resume their pursuit of Serie A's top four when they clash at Stadio Sinigaglia on Sunday.

Both teams are on track to qualify directly for the last 16 in their continental campaigns, but they presently trail Italy's top quartet.

Ascending to third place in the Champions League table - above the likes of Liverpool, Arsenal and Barcelona - Como continued their incredible European exploits on Tuesday evening, with a 1-0 home win over AEK Athens.

Sources indicate that the little Lombardy club are firmly on course to reach the knockout phase on their continental debut, and they are still in an open Serie A title race. Though they recently lost to Inter Milan once again, normal service was resumed last weekend, when Como beat Cagliari 2-0 at the Sinigaglia.

Victory kept them in touch with both Milan sides and the two unbeaten Rome clubs, and the Lariani have claimed a club record 26 points from their first 12 top-flight fixtures.

Unbeaten as hosts this season, Cesc Fabregas has seen his team concede just one goal in five home games, including four consecutive clean sheets - against Roma, Sassuolo, Venezia and Cagliari.

Como now face a crucial clash in the fight for Champions League qualification, and success on Sunday would open up an eight-point lead over Juventus.

Before doing the double over Juve last season, they had not beaten the Turin giants at home since 1952, but a pair of 2-0 wins helped them sneak past the Bianconeri to claim fourth place in the end.

Reflecting their sudden change in status, Juventus have never before faced Como while trailing in the Serie A standings, yet that is now the situation they face.

While the Lariani were dining at Europe’s top table, Juve extended their unbeaten run through this season's Europa League in midweek, defeating Omonia 4-1 in Turin.

Posing a potential solution to their striker problems, Jeff Ekhator found the net on his first start for the club, and across all competitions the Bianconeri have scored 14 goals across their last five games.

In Europe, Juventus are set to cruise through as one of the top eight finishers - having claimed 13 points from a possible 15 so far - but it has been a more mixed picture on the domestic scene.

Despite thumping Venezia 4-0 last week, Luciano Spalletti's injury-hit squad lag 11 points behind league leaders Lazio in sixth place, partly due to their sub-par away form.

Juve’s Serie A record on the road is two wins, two draws and two defeats - with eight goals scored and eight conceded - so visiting Como will surely cause some concern.

Juventus form (all competitions):.

Como are still missing ex-Juventus striker Moise Kean, plus Willy Kambwala and Jesus Rodriguez, but Fabregas could have two wingers back from injury this weekend.

Jayden Addai and Assane Diao both face fitness tests, while midfielder Maxence Caqueret is a strong doubt.

Without Kean, Tasos Douvikas should continue to lead the Lariani’s front line, having scored 11 goals in all competitions this season.

Meanwhile, Juve’s top Serie A scorer is Brazilian centre-back Bremer with a modest three goals, though Nick Woltemade has been directly involved in three across his last two league games and is faring well in the Europa League.

The German striker must compete with Ekhator and Randal Kolo Muani to start at the Sinigaglia, where Spalletti will be without several key men.

Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram and captain Manuel Locatelli are still sidelined, while Nico Gonzalez remains a doubt; more positively, Kerim Alajbegovic and Pierre Kalulu could both be named on the bench.

Butez; Couto, Chalobah, Ramon, Valle; Perrone, Milla; Da Cunha, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas.

Juventus possible starting lineup:.

Vicario; Celik, Bremer, Lucumi, Cabal; Luiz, Koopmeiners; Conceicao, McKennie, Kolo Muani; Woltemade.

Two of Italy's tightest defences will face off on Sunday night: since Spalletti's arrival in Turin last November, Juventus have kept 19 clean sheets and Como have 20.

While the hosts have been far more convincing, Juve are putting together a good run of results and their long absence list is starting to clear.

Latest Update: Arsenal nous frustrates Liverpool as 14-year Anfield hoodoo ends with statement win

📅 02 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5326 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It is clear and obvious that Arsenal will be the team to beat in the Premier League title race, especially given that we do not yet know the fate of faltering Manchester City and their looming punishment.
  • In a recent development, A statement victory against Liverpool, their first in the league at Anfield since 2012, took Arsenal back to the top.
  • Few would when they defend and manage a game – and it was game management in every sense – like this.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It is clear and obvious that Arsenal will be the team to beat in the Premier League title race, especially given that we do not yet know the fate of faltering Manchester City and their looming punishment.

In a recent development, A statement victory against Liverpool, their first in the league at Anfield since 2012, took Arsenal back to the top. And who would bet against them staying there and retaining their title?

Few would when they defend and manage a game – and it was game management in every sense – like this. From the formidable to the cynical – that was the statement. Against the Scousers, Arsenal had the nous.

“The mission was something we didn’t complete in 14 years,” Mikel Arteta said, having famously – in an Amazon documentary series – played You’ll Never Walk Alone to his players as they walked out to train to try and overcome a perceived mental block.

Sources indicate that “There are reasons for that. Some of it psychological, some of it moments we did not nail on the pitch,” the Arsenal manager added of the winless run.

The result means that the north Londoners have already now won away at Villa Park, the Stadium of Light, the City Ground and Anfield. Stadiums where they dropped points last season. And that feels ominous.

It has been revealed that A win would maybe have thrust Liverpool into the title race. Instead, under Andoni Iraola, and with an evolving young team – with promising 19-year-old midfielder Trey Nyoni handed his league debut – they are already nine points behind after just nine matches.

It is also clear, however, that they could have prevented this defeat having somehow been denied a first-half penalty after Alexander Isak’s shirt was blatantly pulled by Jurrien Timber as the striker tried to head home a cross.

It has been revealed that referee Andy Madley may have missed it, but what was the excuse of Stuart Attwell, the VAR? It was a stunningly poor decision – another bad day for Pro Ref and the use of technology.

It might be argued that Timber did not pull hard enough to prevent Isak from reaching the ball. But the defender grabbed the shirt and continued to hold it for a long time. It had to be a penalty. Little wonder Iraola said Isak should dive next time. Who can blame him?

Recent findings suggest that what is also clear and obvious is that, once again, Arsenal’s resilience, defensive determination and appetite for toughing it out will be their greatest weapons. They are certainly, under Arteta, not here to win friends – just to win matches and trophies.

“That defensive line, that togetherness we have is undefeated. It’s something I have never seen before,” Declan Rice, who was also a stand-out performer and delivered a fine assist for the winner, stated.

Arsenal’s version of the Yellow Wall was, indeed, hugely impressive – it is now six clean sheets from their nine league games and, despite all their pressure, Liverpool did not have a shot on target. That has never happened in the Premier League since such statistics started to be compiled in 2003 (422 games ago).

“That’s incredible. It did not feel like it on the pitch. Again, it’s the commitment of every single player,” Arteta said. And that was indisputable.

Even the expected second-half momentum, the expected surge of attack after attack as Liverpool faced the Kop, crashed on Arsenal’s back line. The visitors were so well-drilled that they stifled space – they refused to crumble.

In a recent development, arsenal put their bodies on the line with blocks and tackles and a bit of time-wasting. There were dark arts, especially from both centre-halves with Gabriel going unpunished after claiming he was struck in the face by Isak early on – VAR anyone? – and the otherwise outstanding Ezri Konsa throwing himself to the ground after minimal contact from the Liverpool centre-forward.

According to recent reports, in fairness there was also a bit of that from an increasingly frustrated Liverpool with Alexis Mac Allister going down after touching heads with Noni Madueke, having already tried to provoke Martin Odegaard with a hand to the head when the Arsenal captain was on the turf. That was not good from Mac Allister either.

Recent findings suggest that and the only goal? Again, more frustration for Liverpool. It was well-constructed from Arsenal, but only after Alisson Becker’s loose goal kick, aimed towards Jérémy Jacquet, who was slow to react, was intercepted by Odegaard with Bruno Guimarães poking the ball to the right, where it was collected by Madueke.

Industry observers note that there was an overlap by Rice and his low centre was precise and dangerous across the face of the six-yard area, with Virgil van Dijk unsure what to do. It ran beyond the far post where Kai Havertz side-footed home.

"Absolutely brilliant from Arsenal." Kai Havertz gives Arsenal an early lead at Anfield! ⚡️ https://t.co/eeyhRcLlel.

After that? Liverpool swarmed over Arsenal, particularly in the first-half with Florian Wirtz’s free-kick cannoning back off the crossbar and Mac Allister somehow heading over. He was six yards out and unmarked, it was a glorious chance.

According to recent reports, that was the hosts’ last tangible opportunity to score. As well as Arsenal defended, it was not a good afternoon for Liverpool’s forwards, Bradley Barcola in particular, although it was interesting to see Arsenal double-up on Rio Ngumoha when he came on. Arteta reacted by bringing on a second left-back, in Piero Hincapié.

Arsenal had the best chance with Alisson denying Christos Tzolis as the Greek winger’s low volley threatened to arc around him.

According to recent reports, A brilliant save from Alisson to deny Tzolis! 🧤 https://t.co/0K2DPuUMEu.

It has been revealed that for Liverpool it became frantic. They could not surf the emotion, not against this battle-hardened Arsenal.

Boos rang out at the end – signs of how Arsenal had frustrated Liverpool – as Arteta gained his first win at Anfield as a manager. He was in the last Arsenal team to win here as a player 14 years ago. But this one meant more – that was also clear and obvious as he joyfully jumped into the arms of his assistant, Gabriel Heinze.

"You're supposed to make something of it!" "That's obvious that he's pulled his shirt, why does he need to dive?" Ian Wright and Daniel Sturridge discuss Alexander Isak's penalty appeal 💬 https://t.co/G0aa7tP92t.

"It's a clear penalty" Andoni Iraola is adamant Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty for a foul on Alexander Isak ⤵️ https://t.co/hpaCeVVsbp.

Pride? No disappointment. Disappointment. We played at home. We had some opportunities. Obviously we tried everything. We could have done better in the last 15 minutes to get balls in the box but it wasn’t enough. That’s why it’s a disappointment.

After we conceded we started to play much better. We created the major chance for Alexis which could have changed the game. It didn’t happen. We kept pushing and pushing.

I think there was also a clear penalty. I have seen it back. I’ve seen it being given on other occasions. [Should Alex have made more of it. Maybe the VAR doesn’t notice it…] The VAR doesn’t notice it? We have 50 cameras, even more. Why do you have to complain more if they have 50 cameras. They spotted it because everyone’s seen it. It wasn’t given, we lose the game. Congratulations to Arsenal.

In a recent development, when someone newly introduced comes in the building it just takes a bit if time. Our fans can see there is so much improvement and we work out socks off. What we do need as well is results.

According to recent reports, havertz: “It means a lot to the whole football club. It is key. It’s what they deserve [the fans]. We all know what this stadium is about. We knew it was coming but we all stuck together, defended together. Ninety per cent of the goal belongs to that man [Rice].”.

Industry News: COP31 draft deal calls for 'immediate' shift away from fossil fuels

💡 Key Takeaways
  • COP31 co-host Australia has kicked off the second week of climate talks in Antalya with a draft political deal calling for an "immediate transition away from fossil fuels" and a "tripling" of finance for climate adaptation measures in developing countries to at least $120 billion (€109 billion).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

COP31 co-host Australia has kicked off the second week of climate talks in Antalya with a draft political deal calling for an "immediate transition away from fossil fuels" and a "tripling" of finance for climate adaptation measures in developing countries to at least $120 billion (€109 billion).

According to recent reports, the goal of other co-host Turkey to increase electrification of the world's economies to 35% by 2035 also features in the text. The draft emphasizes clean energy but notes that "electrification can provide co-benefits regardless of the electricity mix" — an approach that has proved divisive at the talks, with many insisting that electrification be strictly tied to renewable energy.

Language around a faster phaseout of oil, coal and gas is key because fossil-fuel producing nations have repeatedly pushed back against stronger wording in previous COP decisions.

"The new negotiating text contains all the necessary building blocks for a successful outcome to the conference: from the goal of climate neutrality for all industrialized countries by 2030 to a work program that can keep the 1.5-degree limit in place," said Greenpeace Germany head Martin Kaiser on Monday.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The draft expressed "deep concern" that the 1.5 Celsius (2.7 Fahrenheit) temperature threshold agreed at the 2015 COP in Paris to avoid runaway climate change was now out of reach. It stressed the need for "accelerating action to minimize both the magnitude and duration of any temperature overshoot and to return global warming to below 1.5C as soon as possible.".

Recognizing a need to address rising carbon emissions, the draft highlighted efforts to "urgently and rapidly" scale up controversial technologies to capture and store CO2 to bring down atmospheric carbon levels.

"For the first time, all the parties here are grappling with the fact that the world will inevitably exceed 1.5 degrees. Negotiators must deliver a response," mentioned Ani Dasgupta, president of the World Resources Institute, adding that this meant going beyond slashing emissions.

"This requires scaling carbon removal through both nature-based solutions like restoring forests and wetlands, or emerging technologies that directly capture carbon from air," he told reporters.

Kaiser, however, criticized the lack of binding commitments in the draft's resolutions. He added that Europe should work with China and the most climate-vulnerable countries to keep oil-producing nations, including Russia and countries in the Middle East, from "undermining the conference's decisions and turning them into a free pass for the oil and gas industry.".

Other activists have dismissed carbon capture as a "false solution" being promoted by corporations.

Cosima Cassel, an expert at climate think tank E3G, was cautiously pleased with the draft's "ambitious language" but said it appeared the broad deal would now leave negotiators to "fight for trade-offs.".

"The test will be whether the final decision keeps the core elements once that process plays out: ambition on overshoot, defense of the science, clean electrification and forward progress on adaptation finance," she said in a statement.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Disagreements over financing largely relate to who should bear the costs of international climate action, whether financial support should be provided through grants or loans, and how funding for developing countries can be increased.

Representatives of developing nations and small island states, regions bearing the brunt of the climate crisis, have protested climate inaction and a lack of financial support in recent days.

"Climate finance isn't an extra at these talks: it's the condition for everything else," remarked Rukiya Khamis, program manager for East Africa with environmental group 350.org. "It's alarming how financial pledges by wealthy, polluting countries are dropping like a stone — COP31 must stop this with a strong outcome on adaptation finance.".

"Now we must fight to keep this [adaption finance] in the final decision and ensure these promises become real, grant-based money," remarked Harjeet Singh of the Fill The Fund campaign, which calls on rich countries and corporations to deliver the funding needed for climate-related loss and damage, such as homes destroyed by floods and harvests ruined by drought.

"Communities are suffering devastating losses and damages today precisely because we failed to deliver adaptation at the right time," added Singh.

Sources indicate that at 18 pages and 144 items, the draft will be the focus of lengthy discussions in the coming days as delegates try to come to an agreement by Friday. Some observers went so far as to say the document's scope was too wide to be taken seriously.

It has been revealed that "The draft final declaration reads like a Christmas wish list," said Niklas Höhne, a climate policy expert at the NewClimate Institute in Germany. "There are even several points on which we will obviously not be able to reach a consensus, including for example the proposal that developed countries achieve net-zero emissions by 2030.".

But Chris Bowen, chief of negotiations and Australia's minister for climate change and energy, appeared optimistic.

"The general tenor and tone [of the talks] has been very constructive," he told reporters Monday. "Parties have come to me with strong views about various things, as you'd expect […] [but] they've also come in the spirit of cooperation, the spirit of respect and a spirit where parties have mentioned to me that they want to help get an outcome.".

David Waskow, director of WRI's International Climate Initiative, said the draft text indicated a level of "seriousness" on important complications like finance, electrification, oceans, overshoot scenarios and emissions of greenhouse gases including methane, which has a warming impact more than 80 times stronger than CO2.

According to recent reports, "The question is whether the level of ambition on those complications is carried through into the final outcome here," said Waskow. "And that's what we need to be watching closely over the coming days.".

Additional reporting by Tim Schauenberg in Antalya.

A guide to the Nature Index

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (780 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Nature Index is a database of author affiliations and institutional relationships.
  • In a recent development, the Nature Index provides absolute and fractional counts of article publication at the institutional and national level and, as such, is an indicator of global high-quality research output and collaboration.
  • It has been revealed that the Nature Index uses Count and Share to track research output.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Nature Index is a database of author affiliations and institutional relationships. The index tracks contributions to research articles published in high-quality natural-science and health-science journals, chosen based on reputation by an independent group of researchers.

In a recent development, the Nature Index provides absolute and fractional counts of article publication at the institutional and national level and, as such, is an indicator of global high-quality research output and collaboration. Data in the Nature Index are updated regularly, with the most recent 12 months made available under a Creative Commons licence at natureindex.com. The database is compiled by Nature Portfolio.

It has been revealed that the Nature Index uses Count and Share to track research output. A country/territory or an institution is given a Count of 1 for each article that has at least one author from that country/territory or institution. This is the case regardless of the number of authors an article has, and it means that the same article can contribute to the Count of multiple countries/territories or institutions.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

To glean a country’s, territory’s, region’s or an institution’s contribution to an article, and to ensure that they are not counted more than once, the Nature Index uses Share, a fractional count that takes into account the share of authorship on each article. The total Share available per article is 1, which is shared among all authors under the assumption that each contributed equally. For instance, an article with 10 authors means that each author receives a Share of 0.1. For authors who are affiliated with more than one institution, the author’s Share is split equally between each institution. The total Share for an institution is calculated by summing the Share for individual affiliated authors. The process is similar for countries/territories, although complicated by the fact that some institutions have overseas labs that will be counted towards host country/territory totals.

Adjusted Share accounts for the annual variation in the total number of articles in the Nature Index journals. It is arrived at by calculating the percentage difference in the total number of articles in the Index in a given year relative to the number of articles in a base year and adjusting Share values to the base year levels.

The bilateral collaboration score (CS) between two institutions A+B is the sum of each of their Shares on the papers to which both have contributed. A bilateral collaboration can be between any two institutions or countries/territories co-authoring at least one article in the journals tracked by the Nature Index.

natureindex.com people can search for specific institutions or countries and generate their own reports, ordered by Count or Share.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03474-5.

The AfD and neo-Nazi networks: How close are the connections?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the electoral successes of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) have brought the party closer than ever to taking power in Germany.
  • This raises an even sharper question: what political ideas does the party stand for, which has been classified by Germany's domestic intelligence agency as a "suspected right-wing extremist" organization and, in several federal states, is already considered "confirmed right-wing extremist"?
  • Many political scientists have observed that the AfD has become increasingly radicalized since its founding in 2013.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the electoral successes of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) have brought the party closer than ever to taking power in Germany. For the 2029 federal election, it has set itself an ambitious goal: to see its co-chair Alice Weidel to become Germany's next chancellor.

This raises an even sharper question: what political ideas does the party stand for, which has been classified by Germany's domestic intelligence agency as a "suspected right-wing extremist" organization and, in several federal states, is already considered "confirmed right-wing extremist"?

Many political scientists have observed that the AfD has become increasingly radicalized since its founding in 2013.

"Viewed as a whole, the AfD is an extreme right-wing party that also displays tendencies associated with a fascist movement," said Fabian Virchow, a researcher on right-wing extremism at Düsseldorf University of Applied Sciences, in an interview with DW.

Industry observers note that virchow identifies different factions and strategic tendencies within the party, some of which are at odds with one another. Party leader Alice Weidel, for example, is generally seen as a proponent of a free-market approach that seeks to keep the state as small as possible. Others, by contrast, favor a strong state shaped by an ethnically homogeneous people, among them Björn Höcke, the influential far-right AfD leader in the state of Thuringia.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that virchow sees a "normalization" of right-wing extremist positions within the AfD. In his view, this has made the party more attractive to neo-Nazi circles: "Today, many people see greater room for ethnonationalist and radical right-wing ideas.".

Support for this observation comes from the latest findings of the Leipzig Authoritarianism Study, one of the most widely cited long-term studies tracking right-wing extremist attitudes in Germany. The researchers behind the study have identified a rise in right-wing extremist views within German society, including a growing acceptance of ideologies rooted in the tradition of National Socialism.

Particularly striking is the finding that around two-thirds of people with firmly entrenched far-right worldviews would vote for the AfD. According to the study, the AfD has achieved what earlier far-right parties in Germany never managed: "to unite large segments of the electorate with anti-democratic attitudes behind it.".

The debate has been further fueled by several recent incidents within the party. In 2026 alone, numerous AfD politicians and staff members made headlines over alleged ties to neo-Nazi organizations:.

In August 2026, police carried out a large-scale raid targeting fifteen people. Authorities suspect them of continuing the activities of the so-called "Artgemeinschaft." Before it was banned in 2023, the group was considered one of Germany's largest and most influential neo-Nazi cadre organizations. Particularly explosive was the fact that two of those targeted in the raid are sitting AfD members of the Saxony-Anhalt state parliament. Their attorneys deny the allegations.

According to reporting by the German daily, Welt, four staff members of the AfD's parliamentary group in Saxony-Anhalt are former members of the now-banned "Heimattreue Deutsche Jugend" (HDJ), a neo-Nazi youth organization rooted in National Socialist racial ideology that organized paramilitary camps for young people. Two of the staff members held leadership positions within the HDJ and now work closely with AfD politician Ulrich Siegmund, who is seeking to become the AfD's first state premier in December.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that remarkably, both organizations, the "Artgemeinschaft" and the HDJ, are on the AfD's so-called incompatibility list, which is intended to draw a line between the party and extremist organizations and movements. In principle, anyone with a history of membership in such groups is supposed to be excluded from the party.

But the list appears to be little more than a dead letter. In 2020, former AfD federal executive board member Andreas Kalbitz was expelled from the party after failing to disclose his membership in the "Heimattreue Deutsche Jugend" on his application to join. Yet according to the news magazine Spiegel, he is once again working for the AfD, this time as a staffer for Saxony-Anhalt state legislator Hans-Thomas Tillschneider, who has since become deputy speaker of the state parliament.

The question of the AfD's relationship to National Socialism has dogged the party since its founding in 2013. Even in its early years, co-founder and first party leader Bernd Lucke sparked controversy when he described democracy and parliamentary politics in Germany as "degenerate," a term the Nazis used to disparage art and culture that did not conform to their ideological worldview.

In Germany, references to the Nazi dictatorship (1933-1945) under Adolf Hitler remain politically taboo because of the country's responsibility for World War Two and the Holocaust, the systematic mass murder of Europe's Jews.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

If AfD members or their staff have come under scrutiny because of past involvement in ethnonationalist or neo-Nazi organizations, they have generally sought to distance themselves from those backgrounds or from the ideologies associated with them.

But how credible are these attempts at distancing? Laura Neumann* has worked with many people seeking to leave the far-right scene. She works for "Nordverbund Ausstieg Rechts," a network of organizations that supports far-right cadres and activists as they disengage from the movement. "A successful exit is the result of a professionally guided process," she remarked in an interview with DW.

It has been revealed that neumann describes leaving the far-right scene as a challenging process of self-confrontation. "When it comes to someone leaving the movement, the first question I always ask is: How does that person talk about their past? Have they genuinely come to terms with it?".

Based on the experience of exit counselors, one principle generally holds true: the longer and more deeply a person has been immersed in far-right circles, the more difficult it becomes to distance themselves from those beliefs and affiliations.

DW requested a statement from the AfD's federal executive board regarding its handling of party members who were previously active in ethnonationalist or neo-Nazi organizations. Individual lawmakers and parliamentary staff members were also asked to comment. None responded.

Recent findings suggest that the party's and its politicians' silence in the face of such allegations reflects an observation made by political scientist Fabian Virchow: "Within the AfD, there is no longer a perceived need to distance oneself from radical far-right positions. That is part of this process of normalization.".

Virchow says that right-wing extremism appears to have advanced so far into the mainstream of German society that efforts to scandalize it now remain largely ineffective.

Sources indicate that * Editor's note: To protect the privacy of the staff member of Nordverbund Ausstieg Rechts, we have changed her name to Laura Neumann. Her real name is known to the editors.

Serie A's sporting judge fined Juventus for holding up the start of the game at Fiorentina, and handed the hosts the same penalty. No Juventus player is banned, so Spalletti has a full squad for Venezia, though Bremer and Kolo Muani now have a sanction against their names.

Industry observers note that juventus came out of their trip to Florence with a bill rather than a ban. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea punished the club for an unjustified delay to the start of the first half at Fiorentina. The hosts were handed an identical penalty for the same hold-up.

According to recent reports, the rulings came in Official Communiqué No. 60, published in Milan on 10 November 2026. Mastrandrea reached them at a meeting that day with Stefania Ginesio and AIA referees’ representative Carlo Moretti. The communiqué states that the fines, including those given to individual club members, will be charged to each club’s LCA league account.

Industry observers note that only one club paid more than Juventus. Como received the heaviest club fine of the round, €10,000, for delaying the start of the second half by about two minutes. The judge treated that as a repeated offence. Genoa were fined €4,000 and Lazio €3,000.

More notable for Spalletti is what the ruling did not contain. No Juventus player was suspended. Only two players across the league were banned after round 11, according to Corriere dello Sport. They were Parma’s Ndiaye and Frosinone’s Bracaglia, each for one match.

According to recent reports, that leaves Spalletti with a full squad for the first game after the international break. He will want every option. The match in Florence, scheduled for Sunday 8 November at 20:45, was assigned to referee Colombo, with Maresca as fourth official and Di Paolo on VAR.

It ended in a draw that left Juventus seventh on 18 points, Eurosport reported. Fiorentina stayed two points clear of the relegation zone. Spalletti said afterwards that his side “are not consistent” and sometimes lose their way over very little.

Sources indicate that the ruling did leave a mark on four first-team figures. Randal Kolo Muani, Gleison Bremer and Juan Cabal each picked up their first sanction of the season. Spalletti’s assistant Marco Domenichini did too.

Bremer and Kolo Muani are key players for the coach.

It has been revealed that the count has only started, but it will matter as the season goes on. The fine itself is small, and the sporting picture is unchanged.

Juventus host Venezia at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 22 November at 12:30.

AC Milan produced a brilliant second-half comeback to overhaul a two-goal deficit and beat Olympiacos 4-2 in the Europa League.

Milan trailed 2-0 after 50 minutes, but Omari Hutchinson was not in the mood to taste more European misery. He scored a brilliant individual goal to get the Rossoneri back into it, before setting up Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic to complete the comeback.

Three goals in 15 crazy minutes overturned the deficit and Diego Moreira made sure of the points late on, helping Ruben Amorim’s side jump into the play-off spots with three games and nine more points up for grabs.

Sources indicate that the general stats makes for interesting reading, as Milan had 59% of the ball and generated 2.25 Expected Goals compared to the 1.56 that their hosts did. They also had 4 big chances to 2, which of course is exactly what the scoreboard reads too.

Last night brought a fourth goal in the Europa League for Alphadjo Cisse, who at the age of 20 years and 35 days has become the youngest player in Milan’s history to score three goals in the major European competitions.

For the first time in their history, Milan have conceded at least two goals in three consecutive matches in Europe’s top competitions.

Olympiakos had lost just one of their last 13 UEFA Europa League matches (W8 D4) before last night, keeping nine clean sheets. In the group stages, they were unbeaten in 11 games (W7 D4), conceding just twice.

The Greek side had also won each of their two previous Europa League contests at the Stadio Georgios Karaiskákis this season, and they had a six-match home unbeaten streak in all competitions broken.

Milan had never won a competitive game against a Greek side in Greece, losing 2 and drawing 4. However, they have lifted the Champions League trophy twice in Athens (4-0 vs. Barcelona in 1994 and 2-1 vs. Liverpool in 2007).

The Rossoneri were scoreless in their last 198 minutes in the competition going into the game in the Europa League, and hadn’t found the net since Gonçalo Ramos’ goal against RB Salzburg. By the time of Hutchinson’s goal, that had reached 254 minutes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After years of speculation, Amazon MGM Studios announced on Monday that Robert Pattinson would be taking on the role of James Bond following Daniel Craig's departure after five hit films in the spy series.

This year alone, Pattinson has starred in "The Odyssey," "The Drama" and "Primetime." He is also famous for his role as "Twilight" vampire Edward Cullen.

The upcoming Bond movie will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, an Oscar nominee known for movies such as the "Dune" trilogy and "Arrival.".

Based on the spy novels by author Ian Fleming, the Bond franchise — about a British secret agent known for his charm and ⁠a ⁠fondness for martinis "shaken, not stirred" — is among the longest-running and highest-grossing in Hollywood history. ​​​​​​​.

In a recent development, the first film in the series, "Dr. No," premiered in London on October 5, 1962.

Playing the leading role, Agent 007, was an unknown actor: Sean Connery.

In the film, we are first introduced to his character as he sits in a casino across from an attractive woman who is about to gamble away her fortune. When she asks 007 his name, the camera pans to Bond lighting a cigarette. With a smoldering look in his eye, he utters the legendary words: "Bond, James Bond.".

According to recent reports, shortly thereafter in the film, 007 receives an assignment to fly to Jamaica and investigate the murder of another M16 agent. He eventually tracks down a Chinese-German criminal scientist who is bent on destroying the US space program and achieving world domination.

In principle, this story is the basis of all of 25 James Bond films. Whether the villain is Dr. No, Blofeld, Goldfinger or Le Chiffre, they all aim for one thing: world domination. But to do so, they have to get past James Bond whose gunfire and wild chase scenes inevitably spoil their aims.

Although many fan forums consider "Dr. No" to be one of the best Bond films, the movie would never be made in the same way today.

Firstly, one could write entire books about the omnipresent sexism and machismo that the character James Bond has displayed over the decades.

Sources indicate that certainly there would have to be a thick chapter dedicated to the women in his films, who are typically portrayed as naive, willingly flinging themselves into Bond's arms, seeking protection. Sometimes they are sophisticated female antagonists who lose control at the thought of hopping into bed with the secret agent.

Whether friend of foe, each film had at least one Bond girl — and often more: More than 60 love interests have appeared in the films. Their names, like "Honey" or "Pussy Galore" would never be acceptable today. In more recent decades, female roles in Bond films have changed — as has Bond himself.

In the last five films in which Daniel Craig has played Bond, he is seen as a man who is tough on the outside and soft on the inside — and who is not always lucky with women.

In a recent development, aside from the portrayal of women on screen, there are also plenty of other details in "Dr. No" that haven't quite stood the test of time.

Another sign of the zeitgeist in the 1962 film is that everyone smokes, which is a no-no by today's Hollywood standards. Cigarettes are found everywhere in the old film, from the casino to the hotel bar — and even the bedroom.

It has been revealed that smoking was commonplace in the US in the 1970s, so naturally this came across on the silver screen. In the 1970s TV series "Space: 1999" people were even depicted smoking on the moon, but by the 2000s, smoking was largely banned in many parts of the world due to its health risks.

Sources indicate that one can also note in "Dr. No" that few people are wearing seat belts. When Bond drives off in his sports car to visit a woman, he is followed and a chase scene ensues. Bond, notably, is not wearing a seat belt.

According to recent reports, his pursuers eventually drive off a slope and die, of course — after all, they aren't wearing seat belts either and cars didn't have airbags at the time. The vehicle explodes, prompting 007 to say, "They were obviously in a hurry to get to their own funeral.".

In the older Bond films, all secretaries and receptionists are played by women, which in the 1960s, were considered standard female jobs.

Whether redheaded, blonde or brunette, secretaries are Bond's favorite targets for womanizing and they are all susceptible to his charms.

Throughout most Bond films, the agent has a romantic tension with Moneypenny, his boss's secretary, something which was not described in the original books.

In the 2012 film "Skyfall" Moneypenny is given a first name: Eve, and we finally learn her backstory. In this film, she is no longer a hopeless secretary in love, but a top-trained agent who accidentally shoots Bond and is reassigned to desk duty as punishment.

In any case, today Moneypenny's job title today would probably be "Office Manager" or "Executive Assistant" rather than "Secretary.".

In the film, Dr. No tells James Bond that he is the child of a British missionary and a Chinese woman from an upstanding family. However, the character is portrayed by Canadian actor Joseph Wiseman who is wearing makeup to make his eyes look more "Asian.".

While it used to be the norm in such movies to have East Asian characters played by white actors, today these cases of "yellowface" are frowned upon — just as it would be to wear blackface, putting black makeup on one's skin to portray a Black person.

If there was a "Dr. No" remake in the future, a Chinese actor would be more likely to play this role.

Daniel Craig already paved the way in modernizing James Bond by stripping away campy gadgets, punchlines and invincibility, replacing them with a grounded, psychological and emotionally vulnerable portrayal of a post-9/11 spy.

Now it is up to Robert Pattinson to revisit the famous MI6 agent. Film critics believe his background will allow him to add dark sophistication and nonconformism to the iconic espionage role.

Throughout his career, Robert Pattinson has managed to combine roles in blockbuster hits and indie gems, from Bruce Wayne in "The Batman" to a disposable worker who is cloned every time he dies in "Mickey 17.".

Pattinson already has experience with classic spy archetypes: As the mysterious Neil in Christopher Nolan's sci-fi action thriller "Tenet," he assisted the protagonist in a time-bending espionage mission. He is also known for his eccentric personality and deadpan humor — qualities that could be useful for a modern Bond.

It has been revealed that this article was translated from German by Sarah Hucal. It was first published in 2025 and updated following news of Robert Pattinson's casting as James Bond on November 16, 2026.

Recent findings suggest that eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino. With the league's penalty rate down and the team seventh, the João Mario handball in Florence has become the clearest example of a call that went against them.

Juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches. Seven sides are still waiting for a penalty in their favour: Roma, Juventus, Torino, Lecce, Fiorentina, Sassuolo and Udinese. Seven have yet to concede one: Inter, Milan, Como, Juventus, Napoli, Torino and Genoa. Only the two Turin clubs appear on both lists.

It has been revealed that that makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks. Sportmediaset puts the number of teams still waiting for a penalty partly down to the upcoming refereeing approach introduced by Orsato.

Sources indicate that the wider numbers show a quieter season from the spot. The 24 penalties so far work out at about 0.22 per match, compared with 0.28 and 0.27 in the two previous seasons. The drop was sharpest early on. Only five of the 24 penalties came in the first five rounds.

Sources indicate that the trend has not been flat since then. The rate rose to 0.31 per match after the September international break. Juventus have not shared in that rise. Their total in both columns remains zero.

Industry observers note that the contrast with last season is clear. Juventus were awarded five league penalties then. They also had the last three saved: David’s against Lecce, Yildiz’s against Cremonese and Locatelli’s against Sassuolo.

Sources indicate that the case that has drawn most attention came late in the 2-2 draw at Fiorentina. João Mario handled the ball. No penalty was given. Gianluca Rocchi, who now works as a DAZN pundit, said it should have been a spot-kick. His reasoning was that the arm was out wide and the player had time to move it, even though the ball came from a teammate.

Luciano Spalletti signalled that he also saw a penalty. He chose not to complain publicly about the decision.

Close calls carry weight at this stage. Juventus are seventh on 18 points, six behind fourth place. Champions League qualification is in doubt. An injury-hit squad cannot easily absorb lost points from decisions at the margins.

Recent findings suggest that the run after the break will test whether the pattern holds. Venezia, the next league opponents, are among five clubs to have conceded three penalties, the league’s highest total. Frosinone, Bologna, Atalanta and Sassuolo share that figure. Sassuolo are also on the list of sides yet to be awarded one.

Industry observers note that the schedule is crowded. After Venezia, Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League. A league trip to Como follows, then Sassuolo at home in the Coppa Italia. Como have yet to concede a penalty this season.

Sources indicate that the first of those fixtures has already moved. Lega Serie A brought Juventus v Venezia forward to Sunday 22 November at 12:30, from its original slot on Monday 23 November at 20:45.

Industry observers note that tzolis started the first five league games, then suffered a hamstring injury on international duty. Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke have covered since, and Madueke rescued a point in Saturday’s 2-2 draw at Newcastle, which left Arsenal six points clear for now.

Nusa, the 21-year-old Norwegian winger, has six goals and eight assists in 15 matches for Leipzig. Sky Sports reports that the Bundesliga club won’t sell him in January, so a summer deal looks more realistic, with Leipzig reportedly valuing him between £60m and £77m. Schade is the quicker route, but Arsenal asked about him in the summer and got nowhere, according to TEAMtalk. His contract runs until 2028.

It has been revealed that schade has scored three times in ten Premier League appearances from 2.44 expected goals, and his pace suits a side that already creates through Tzolis. He can play either flank or centrally. The weaknesses show elsewhere: no assists, three chances created in 781 minutes, seven completed dribbles at a 25% success rate and 43.8% of duels won. FotMob values him at about £47m.

Industry observers note that not in January, and certainly not as a consolation. Arsenal lead the league, Tzolis remains the first-choice left winger, and Madueke has just shown he can deliver there. Schade would add depth, but he wouldn’t add what Arteta lacks: a winger who beats his man and drags two defenders with him against low blocks.

Sources indicate that nusa builds his game on exactly that, and his output at Leipzig now justifies waiting until next summer. Schade’s returns suggest he would sit behind a fit Tzolis, which is hard to justify at a price Brentford would set after already refusing an approach.

A bid becomes sensible only if Tzolis breaks down again or Leipzig block Nusa completely, because Schade needs no time to adapt to the Premier League. Even then, anything above £50m would pay for potential rather than production, and a 25% dribble success rate tells Arsenal he isn’t the specialist they need.

Porto will look to maintain their perfect start to the league season when they welcome Sporting Lisbon to Estadio do Dragao for Sunday's matchday 12 headline fixture.

The Dragons have won all 11 of their league matches to sit top of the Primeira Liga table, five points clear of second-placed Benfica and nine ahead of the third-placed Lions.

Francesco Farioli has made an impressive start to his second season in charge of Porto after leading the team to the title last term, and the Dragons are now just two victories away from matching their best start to a top-flight campaign, having won their first 13 matches in 1939-40.

The Blue and Whites, who recorded a league-high 21 clean sheets and conceded just 18 goals in the Primeira Liga last campaign, have maintained their defensive solidity this term, allowing a league-low five goals and registering the joint-most shutouts (six).

Porto's most recent outing in the Portuguese top flight was a hard-fought 2-1 victory over Vitoria de Guimaraes, in an encounter where Martim Fernandes scored an 86th-minute winner to preserve the Dragons' flawless record in the top flight.

Farioli's men have also put their continental campaign back on track, with a 1-0 victory away to Feyenoord in midweek marking their second consecutive Champions League win and lifting the Blue and Whites to 22nd in the 36-team table after they lost their opening three fixtures in the competition.

Porto have now won six of their last seven matches across all competitions in regulation time, with the only exception being a penalty shootout victory over lower-division Paredes to reach the last 16 of the Taca de Portugal, where they will face Leiria on December 17.

Looking to extend their perfect league run, Farioli’s charges can also draw confidence from their impressive home form, having won all five of their Primeira Liga matches at the Dragao this season while scoring at least twice in each, including a 3-1 success over Benfica in September's O Classico.

However, Sporting have the opportunity to become the latest major obstacle in that pursuit, with the visitors arriving with renewed confidence following their recent managerial change, which saw Paulo Fonseca replace Rui Borges in early November.

The 53-year-old, who previously managed Porto during the 2013-14 campaign, oversaw a 1-0 league win over Moreirense in his first game in charge of his current club, with Luis Suarez scoring the winner, before guiding the Lions to another victory in the Taca de Portugal against Uniao de Serra.

Sporting's most recent outing was a chaotic 2-2 draw with Manchester United on Wednesday, leaving the Lisbon outfit ninth in the Champions League table while extending their unbeaten run to five matches (W4, D1) across all competitions.

The Lions have also avoided defeat in all five of their league away games this season (W3, D2), but Sunday's clash presents a different challenge, given they have managed just two victories in their last 19 Primeira Liga meetings (D9, L8) with Porto and are winless in their last 10 top-flight visits to the Dragao (D5, L5), drawing each of the most recent three.

Sporting Lisbon Primeira Liga form:.

Sporting Lisbon form (all competitions):.

Porto will be without Gabriel Mec, Vasco Sousa (broken leg) and former Manchester United defender Chris Smalling (knee) as they continue their respective recoveries from injury.

Santiago Gimenez led the line in the victory over Feyenoord, but Samu Aghehowa could reclaim the number nine spot following his starts in the Dragons' last two league matches, although Andre Silva remains in contention, having recorded more minutes than the other two forwards in the Primeira Liga this season.

As for Sporting, Zeno Debast and Nuno Santos returned to training earlier in the week following spells on the sidelines, although this encounter could come too soon for both players.

Luis Suarez is expected to lead the line once again, with the Colombian, who won the Golden Boot with 28 league goals last season, having already found the net nine times in the Primeira Liga this term, leaving him two behind Benfica's Vangelis Pavlidis.

Porto possible starting lineup:.

D Costa; A Costa, Bednarek, Kiwior, Sanusi; G Veiga, Rosario, Froholdt; Sainz, Samu, Pepe.

Sporting Lisbon possible starting lineup:.

K Pereira; Fresneda, Quaresma, Inacio, Araujo; Andersen, Altimira, Doumbia; Catamo, Suarez, Guilherme.

Heavyweight derbies such as this are difficult to call, regardless of form or momentum, and Sporting's recent performances suggest they have enough quality to make life uncomfortable for the league leaders.

Furthermore, three of the last five meetings between the sides across all competitions have ended in draws so we are backing another stalemate, which would bring the Dragons' flawless league run to an end.
