⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Everton Under-21s' Jersey Mikes Trophy campaign ended with a third straight group stage defeat at the hands of Tranmere Rovers.
  • Everton Under-21s' Jersey Mikes Trophy campaign ended with a third straight group stage defeat at the hands of Tranmere Rovers.
  • The Prenton Park tie was a dead rubber with Everton already eliminated and Rovers already through to the knockout stage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Everton Under-21s' Jersey Mikes Trophy campaign ended with a third straight group stage defeat at the hands of Tranmere Rovers. The Prenton Park tie was a dead rubber with Everton already eliminated and Rovers already through to the knockout stage. Charlie Veevers created an early opening for the home side on the left edge of the Everton box but his shot was deflected wide for a corner. The Blues' first opening came after a quarter of an hour. Rovers midfielder Sam Finley played a sloppy pass straight to Malik Olayiwola but the final effort from distance was blocked. Everton took the lead five minutes later when Olayiwola played in Braiden Graham who was sharp enough to get to the ball before Coniah Boyce-Clarke and poke it into the net.There was a chance for Tranmere to hit back promptly but Veevers and David Kamara contrived to get in each other's way inside the Everton penalty area and the former lashed his shot well wide of the target. Shortly after, Olayiwola’s flick provided Graham with another sight of goal but this time the best he could do was win a corner. The hosts levelled just before the break when Kamara timed his forward run well enough to just stay onside before steering a neat finish past Fraser Barnsley. There was a touch of good fortune to the goal that gave Rovers the lead early in the second half and ultimately secured the victory. Veevers' effort would probably have been covered by Barnsley had it not taken a nick off Will Tamen on the way. Kamara tested Barnsley from a narrow angle on 62 minutes and from the subsequent corner kick Ryan Watson headed over, and at the other end Melvin Matos was desperately unfortunate to see his superbly struck shot strike the Rovers crossbar.To their credit, Everton stuck at it and kept themselves in the game. Olayiwola was next to try his luck but from distance he thumped the ball high over the bar. Two Everton substitutes combined well with 10 minutes remaining. Shea Pita played a beautifully weighted pass into the path of George Finney who surprised Boyce-Clarke with a first-time shot that the keeper gathered at the second attempt. Boyce-Clarke had to be alert again in added time to keep out a snapshot volley from Matos. Speaking after the game, Head of Academy Player Development Dave Hughes told evertonfc.com: "If you look at the first half performance, we thought we were worthy of being a goal up. The progress from the first (Jersey Mikes Trophy) game at Stockport to tonight is clear in terms of more maturity and better decision-making in the way they try to play. "Towards the end of the game we were still pushing forward and trying to get an equaliser but the reality of it is for the boys to get to where they want to be, they’ve got to find a way to win. "We looked composed with the ball and we were on the front foot but at the end of the game experience showed and they managed the critical moments better, which is where we’ve got to improve and we’ll keep nursing the lads along. "(In) the first 15 minutes of the second half they came at us quite quickly and we switch off from a throw-in which leads to a goal, but we feel that we are making progress. Harvey Foster was excellent in the first half, Will Tamen was outstanding and there were some really good performances so we’re really pleased. "Melvin Matos is relentless. He’s got this unbelievable knack of pressing the life out of people and closing the space very quickly. If he can get his first touch out of his feet and run at the backline, he’s a threat. "He’s developing nicely. He’s got plenty of work still to do but with all the guys their appetite to work and seek improvement and develop has been outstanding. "We tell them that if you want a career in the game then winning is essential and you need the mentality to keep improving your performance. Within that as individuals you have to show grit and steel and play with character and personality.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Flamengo director José Boto insists the Brazilian club will sell Roma-linked Samuel Lino only for a ‘very high offer’ but refuses to confirm Giallorossi interest.

Recent findings suggest that several sources report that Flamengo wing-back Samuel Lino is on Roma’s shopping list. Earlier this week, RTI Esporte even claimed that the Giallorossi were ready to submit a €45m bid for the 26-year-old.

“Several clubs are interested, but I won’t say whether Roma is among them,” Flamengo director Boto told TMW.

“I can confirm that the interest in him is concrete, and we receive inquiries about the player every day. We bought Lino at a favourable age for a possible future sale. We paid €25m for him, and obviously we won’t sell him for less. I don’t even know if we’ll sell him at all, unless we receive a very high offer.”.

Samuel Lino joined Flamengo from Atletico Madrid in the summer of 2025.

The Brazil international has scored 13 goals and provided nine assists in 35 appearances in the Brazilian Serie A this season.

Roma already did business with Flamengo in recent years, signing Brazilian full-back Wesley for €25m plus add-ons in 2025. The Brazilian club used the proceeds from Wesley’s sale to sign Samuel Lino from Atletico Madrid.

Roma sit second in the Serie A table with 30 points from 12 matches and are the only unbeaten team, alongside their city rivals Lazio, who lead the table.

Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (774 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Another key opposition media outlet in Turkey has been placed under state control.
  • Industry observers note that A trustee has also been appointed: The state deposit protection fund, TMSF, which usually administers the assets of insolvent companies, has been put in charge.
  • According to recent reports, A large police contingent raided the broadcaster's headquarters in Istanbul, with counterterrorism officers searching the offices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Another key opposition media outlet in Turkey has been placed under state control. On Tuesday morning, authorities raided the offices of the television broadcaster Sozcu TV and the news portal Sozcu.com.tr, and arrested several executives.

Industry observers note that A trustee has also been appointed: The state deposit protection fund, TMSF, which usually administers the assets of insolvent companies, has been put in charge. Sozcu was one of the last big media companies in Turkey to regularly report critically on the government of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

According to recent reports, A large police contingent raided the broadcaster's headquarters in Istanbul, with counterterrorism officers searching the offices. According to Sozcu, its chairwoman, Funda Tuncer Sidali, and Asim Akgul, the former chief executive of the Sozcu group, were among those arrested.

The broadcaster did not initially announce the appointment of the trustee on its digital channels. It did call on its audience to follow it under a new account. The leader of the main opposition party, Ozgur Ozel, declared on X: "You will never be able to prevent this nation's voice from rising, its rebellion from being heard, its cry from echoing.".

The Istanbul public prosecutor's office has confirmed the arrangements. It justified the investigation with claims of a suspected connection between the owner of Sozcu, Burak Akhay, and the Gülen movement. The Turkish government blames this movement, which was once allied to Erdogan, for the attempted coup in 2016, and has designated it a terrorist organization.

It has been revealed that according to the investigators, Akbay is said to have used foreign bank accounts to finance two companies involved in media activities on behalf of the Gülen movement. They claim there is strong suspicion that he was able, in this way, to hold a leadership position in the organization.

It has been revealed that it is not newly introduced for the Turkish state to take over media organizations by appointing trustees. Many media companies accused of being close to the Gülen movement were brought under state control in this way after the attempted coup in 2016. What is new is that for about a year now this is also happening to media seen as pro-opposition.

Sozcu is not the first opposition broadcaster to be targeted by the authorities. The TELEI TV channel was searched on October 24, 2025. Its editor-in-chief, Merdan Yanardag, was arrested on charges of espionage and remains in custody. The offices of Halk TV were raided on October 14 this year. There, too, a trustee was put in charge.

In the space of just over a year, three of the most important opposition television channels have been brought under state control. Observers see this as another step toward an increasingly authoritarian and politically isolated system.

Berk Esen, a political scientist with Sabanci University in Istanbul, sees these measures as a significant weakening of the opposition in the public domain.

Esen told DW that the government may first have acted behind the scenes and tried to bring Sozcu to heel politically. When this didn't succeed, it invoked the judiciary. Esen notes Turkey is increasingly moving toward an authoritarian system. The attempt to prevent opposition organizations and media from gaining strength and influence is part of this.

Sources indicate that esen describes the opposition's success in local government elections in March 2024 as a political turning point. Since then, he indicates, the government has seen its chances of winning political competitions at the ballot box receding. "It's become harder for the AKP to win elections," says Esen. "That's why it's attacking the opposition and the free media both at once.".

Sources indicate that several opposition mayors have also been arrested in recent months and replaced by trustees. They include the mayor of Istanbul and presidential candidate Ekrem Imamoglu, who has been in detention since his arrest in March last year. He is regarded as one of Erdogan's most promising challengers.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The Turkish Journalists' Association (TGC) spoke of a "black winter for press freedom," and confirmed its solidarity with all those affected. It described the recent developments as a serious attack on press freedom. The fact that a trustee had been appointed, first at Halk TV and now at Sozcu, demonstrated how the media climate in Turkey has deteriorated, it said.

"These days, too, shall pass," the TGC declared. "When that day comes, those journalists who seek the truth today will be remembered, as will the decisions that prevent the public from hearing that truth.".

From young players to women's game to the national team, how can SFA duo Maxwell and Mulholland possibly be trusted to move things forward?

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1506 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 13:33 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 15:30 EST, 27 November 2026.
  • With the Scottish FA’s widely trumpeted plan to get young players more game time now lying in a ditch off the M74, it was hard not to raise a wry smile at the midweek communique from Hampden over the intention to come up with some other kind of just-as-good idea somewhere in the newly introduced year.
  • ‘Given the implications for our game, and our young talent, it is imperative that we take the necessary time to get those proposals right,’ it closed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 13:33 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 15:30 EST, 27 November 2026.

With the Scottish FA’s widely trumpeted plan to get young players more game time now lying in a ditch off the M74, it was hard not to raise a wry smile at the midweek communique from Hampden over the intention to come up with some other kind of just-as-good idea somewhere in the newly introduced year.

‘Given the implications for our game, and our young talent, it is imperative that we take the necessary time to get those proposals right,’ it closed.

According to recent reports, bit late for that chat, is it not? Shouldn’t that work behind the scenes have been done before the grand summit at St Andrews back at the start of September when SFA chief executive Ian Maxwell and his chief football officer Craig Mulholland announced themselves lords and saviours of the national game with their scheme to shoehorn Under-21 players – no matter how good, bad or indifferent they may be – into club sides all over the country?

It all sounded good at the time, of course, if you put your head in the clouds and daydreamed over how pretty the world might be if everyone just got along.

Handwringers nationwide fell over themselves to simper the usual platitudes over how self-interest must be sacrificed for the greater good. There was probably some kind of online petition to link hands between all 42 senior grounds for a chorus of Kumbaya.

Meanwhile, anyone who has the faintest idea of the realpolitik of Scottish football looked at what was on the table and knew it was destined for the knacker’s yard.

SFA top brass Craig Mulholland and Ian Maxwell flank Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli.

The SFA should have been consulting their more prominent clubs before going public over what might work and what might not, moulding something that the teams which matter were willing to support.

Instead, almost half the outfits in the Premiership blew their proposals out of the water in the end.

The sound of silence from Hampden, of course, had already become deafening as they realised they’d made a pig’s ear of it. Right now, it looks like everyone is back to the drawing board.

Recent findings suggest that it’s embarrassing for the SFA. It has just made Maxwell and Mulholland look like they are incapable of taking the game with them on important matters.

Naturally, though, there wasn’t a single word from Haudit or Daudit in that press release to more or less confirm a major reverse ferret is going to be required. When things go belly-up, the high heid yins at Hampden are often nowhere to be seen.

Maxwell was too busy turning his mind to other matters during the week anyway, namely the fact that Scotland will be co-hosting the Women’s World Cup with the rest of the UK in 2035.

Given that was the only actual bid, the award of the event was hardly earth-shattering, but that didn’t stop Maxwell treating it as his Next Big Thing.

Maxwell has been in position at the SFA for more than eight years but has lacked real impact.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I think it is going to be an absolutely transformational event to host in the UK and Ireland,’ he gushed. ‘The hard work starts now in terms of legacy and impact and driving everything we can from it.’.

It has been revealed that hmmmm. Nice as it is that he’s managed to put being custard-pied at home by a large chunk of the Premiership over youth opportunities behind him, it might be wise to take Maxwell’s words over the women’s game with a pinch of salt.

He also called Scotland going to their first World Cup in 2019 ‘transformational’. Months later, Glasgow City won their 13th straight title with a ten-goal win over Motherwell on a council-run pitch in Wishaw in front of 100 people with no shelter, no seating and no obvious way for an ambulance to gain entry should a medical emergency occur. One Motherwell player had to nick across to the attached sports centre to get a chair for an injured team-mate to sit on.

A year had passed since the national team’s qualification, but there was still no kind of proposal for the £400,000 prize money that they earned.

City’s Hayley Lauder, who’d been at the World Cup in France, tweeted: ‘Just won a league title in a public park at a sports centre. Not how I envisaged the game in 2019.’.

It was a message that encapsulated the catastrophic failure to build on the incredible platform France 2019 provided under Maxwell’s reign.

Scotland celebrate an Erin Cuthbert goal against Argentina in 2019 before it all turned sour.

It has been revealed that that should have been the real launchpad for the women’s game here. Instead, it turned into a toxic shambles that killed any kind of momentum.

Industry observers note that progress since has been nothing like what it should have been. The national team, out to reach the next World Cup in next week’s play-off against Sweden, has been mired in failure. The women’s game lives back in the shadows amid pitiful attendances and an inability – or, it sometimes seems, refusal – to sell itself.

Yet, it could all have been so different. Just remember the scene back in ‘19. Scotland have to beat Argentina to make the last 16. A TV audience of six million watched the meeting with England earlier in the campaign.

The drama as Shelley Kerr’s side let slip a three-goal lead with 16 minutes to play – eventually drawing 3-3 thanks to a stoppage-time penalty retaken after an initial save by keeper Lee Gibson – was just incredible. It was the talk of the nation the next day.

And, then, it all just died a death. The head coach Shelley Kerr eventually coughed to the fact ‘a few drinks’ had been taken before a debrief the next day that reportedly left some players in tears.

No one wanted to talk about it. No one ever has, really. Yours truly asked Glasgow City for an interview with Gibson, then Alexander, in the early stages of the following season.

Top-flight matches between teams in the SWPL regularly take place on glorified public pitches.

She’d been at the centre of a major global event. There was a story to be told. City insisted all requests had to be run past the SFA and their media office pretty much made it clear it wouldn’t be happening before she had even been asked.

Recent findings suggest that no one told their stories of the biggest event in the history of women’s football here. Not properly. It felt like some kind of Omerta had been put in place over it.

It has been revealed that kerr, inexplicably, was allowed to keep her job by Maxwell and then failed to make it to Euro 2022. Instead, that year was marked by the women’s team, with Kerr gone, threatening to take legal action against the SFA over a lack of resources – with then captain Rachel Corsie referring to ‘years of iniquity, disrespect, and, in some cases, abuse.’.

Yeah, the aftermath of France 2019 was ‘transformational’ all right. It transformed the hundreds of thousands of folk compelled to watch women’s football on national TV that summer back into people who forget it even exists.

Industry observers note that colleagues tell me there was no scope midweek to even interview anyone in a position of power within the SFA over what should have been a Good News Story regarding 2035. Hardly ‘driving everything we can from it’, is it?

I mean, how can you trust the likes of Maxwell to harness the opportunities afforded by that event – or Euro 2028 on home soil – when reflecting upon the raging binfire France 2019 became?

Mulholland is a regular sight being entertained by football matches up and down the country.

How can you trust him and Mulholland to get it right on forging pathways for young players when they made such a Horlicks of trying to implement that poorly-planned proposal for Scotland-eligible Under-21s and failed again when changing it to involve Under-23s?

There’s a far wider issue with the production of players that involves going deep into the SFA’s own workings, addressing that lack of knowledge St Mirren boss Craig McLeish talked about at the lower levels of grassroots.

Indeed, there are problems all over the SFA. With refereeing standards. With VAR. With Steve Clarke admitting he forced the top brass into ‘panicking’ before the World Cup and giving him a latest four-year deal.

If Maxwell and Mulholland’s blue-eyed boy Sebastien Pocognoli doesn’t start looking like he’s got a handle on his role as Clarke’s successor as national boss after a grim start to his reign, everything points to the two of them having to go the same way as their original Youth Initiative. By being binned.

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Liverpool City Council has approved an updated Liverpool Waters masterplan, marking another significant milestone in the regeneration of the city’s northern waterfront and building on the transformation brought about by the development of Everton’s Hill Dickinson Stadium.
  • Liverpool City Council has approved an updated Liverpool Waters masterplan, marking another significant milestone in the regeneration of the city’s northern waterfront and building on the transformation brought about by the development of Everton’s Hill Dickinson Stadium.
  • The revised planning framework, brought forward by Peel Waters, will guide the next phase of development across the 60-hectare site stretching from Everton's headquarters at The Royal Liver Building to the Club’s fresh waterfront home at Bramley-Moore Dock.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool City Council has approved an updated Liverpool Waters masterplan, marking another significant milestone in the regeneration of the city’s northern waterfront and building on the transformation brought about by the development of Everton’s Hill Dickinson Stadium. The revised planning framework, brought forward by Peel Waters, will guide the next phase of development across the 60-hectare site stretching from Everton's headquarters at The Royal Liver Building to the Club’s new waterfront home at Bramley-Moore Dock. The development of Hill Dickinson Stadium has acted as a catalyst for the regeneration of North Liverpool, stimulating investment, creating employment opportunities, attracting visitors and unlocking the potential of a previously underutilised area of the city. The updated masterplan reflects the significant changes that have taken place along Liverpool’s waterfront since the original planning consent was granted in 2013, most notably the development of Everton’s new home and its emergence as a major sporting, entertainment and visitor destination. The refreshed prepares will support the delivery of new homes, including affordable housing, alongside high-quality public spaces, healthcare provision, community facilities, employment opportunities and sustainable infrastructure across five distinctive waterfront neighbourhoods. Central to the plans is the creation of a new five-acre waterfront park at Central Docks. Already under construction as part of Liverpool Waters’ £81 million infrastructure investment programme, the park will feature more than 3,000 trees and is expected to open in spring 2028. The park and wider development will provide new and enhanced pedestrian routes through the northern docks, offering supporters and visitors an optional attractive walking route between Liverpool city centre and Hill Dickinson Stadium. Alongside new leisure and hospitality destinations, the creation of these public spaces will help transform the matchday and non-matchday journey for Evertonians, providing more opportunities for supporters to spend time along the waterfront before and after fixtures and major events at the stadium. The increased focus on pedestrian connectivity, active travel and sustainable transport also complements Everton’s ongoing work with key stakeholders to improve accessibility to Hill Dickinson Stadium and better connect the Club’s waterfront home with the city centre and surrounding communities.Colin Chong, Everton’s Chief Real Estate and Regeneration Officer, stated: “From the outset, our ambition for Hill Dickinson Stadium extended far beyond delivering a new home for Everton Football Club. It was also about unlocking the potential of Liverpool’s northern waterfront and providing a catalyst for wider investment, regeneration and economic growth. “We are already seeing the positive impact of the stadium on the surrounding area, with new businesses establishing themselves and existing businesses benefiting from increased footfall and activity. “The updated Liverpool Waters masterplan provides an opportunity to build on that momentum. New public spaces, improved walking routes and better connectivity will complement our own investment in establishing Hill Dickinson Stadium and our Budweiser Plaza as a year-round destination, enhancing the appeal of the area, attracting more visitors and creating further opportunities for businesses, investment and employment across North Liverpool.” The growing programme of major sporting and entertainment events at Hill Dickinson Stadium is extending the economic benefits of Everton’s investment beyond football matchdays and across the wider Liverpool City Region. As well as being the home for Everton's Premier League fixtures, Hill Dickinson Stadium has already hosted an international football fixture between Scotland and Côte d’Ivoire, a Rugby League Ashes Test, Magic WKND and a Rugby Union Nations Championship fixture, the stadium will also host matches during UEFA EURO 2028, with a programme of major concerts at the Club’s waterfront home set to get under way in summer 2027. The ability to attract events of national and international significance is helping to further strengthen Liverpool’s reputation as a global sporting, cultural and entertainment destination, drawing additional visitors to the city, supporting its hotel, hospitality, retail and transport sectors, and creating further opportunities for investment and employment across the region. Since the original Liverpool Waters masterplan was approved in 2013, the northern waterfront has undergone significant change, with the delivery of new residential developments, transport infrastructure, leisure and hospitality destinations and public spaces, alongside Hill Dickinson Stadium and the Isle of Man Ferry Terminal. James Whittaker, Managing Director of Peel Waters, said: “The approval of the updated Liverpool Waters masterplan marks another major milestone in the transformation of Liverpool’s northern waterfront. Since the original masterplan was approved in 2013, we have delivered significant progress across the site, including new homes, public spaces, leisure destinations, major transport infrastructure and the new Everton Stadium, helping establish Liverpool Waters as one of the UK’s most ambitious regeneration projects. “This updated framework reflects the considerable investment already made by Peel Waters and our partners, while providing the flexibility needed to respond to evolving market demand and future opportunities. With over £81 million of infrastructure investment committed at Central Docks, Princes Dock nearing completion and a clear vision for future neighbourhoods, Liverpool Waters is entering an exciting new chapter that will continue to create homes, jobs, investment and opportunities for Liverpool and the wider city region.” The revised framework also strengthens commitments around sustainability, biodiversity, climate resilience and the preservation of Liverpool’s rich maritime heritage – principles that were central to the development of Everton’s waterfront home. Pete Swift, CEO and Co-Founder, Planit – the landscape architecture, urban design and masterplanning studio who also worked as part of the team to deliver Everton's new home, added: “We are overjoyed at the approval, not just for the Peel Waters and Liverpool Waters team but for the communities of Liverpool. “A network of green and blue spaces, with the central park at the heart, now forms the backbone for our neighbourhoods. We understand better the assets that sit below the ground and the history on and above it – views old and new structure the place. “Hill Dickinson stadium changes the game; literally – for Everton Football Club and North Liverpool. It was never in the original masterplan [from 2013] and so we must adapt to respond to it and the opportunities it brings. Our wider variety of homes now represents a more inclusive, family-focused, inter-generational Liverpool Waters. “Today’s consent embodies Peel Waters’ future-facing attitude and commitment to the quality of buildings and their supporting infrastructure – to remake a place that will play a major role in North Liverpool’s sustainable future.” The approved masterplan retains Liverpool Waters’ five-neighbourhood structure comprising Princes Dock, KINGS, Central Docks, Clarence Docks and Northern Docks. Liverpool Waters also sits within the proposed Liverpool City Region Mayoral Development Zone, an initiative designed to accelerate regeneration, support investment and unlock the delivery of new homes, jobs and infrastructure. The approval of Peel Waters' updated masterplan represents the next stage in the evolution of Liverpool’s northern waterfront, building on the investment made by Everton in delivering Hill Dickinson Stadium and the Club’s longstanding ambition for its new home to be a driver of economic growth, regeneration and lasting opportunities for North Liverpool and the wider city region.

Alongside new leisure and hospitality destinations, the creation of these public spaces will help transform the matchday and non-matchday journey for Evertonians, providing more opportunities for supporters to spend time along the waterfront before and after fixtures and major events at the stadium.

The increased focus on pedestrian connectivity, active travel and sustainable transport also complements Everton’s ongoing work with key stakeholders to improve accessibility to Hill Dickinson Stadium and better connect the Club’s waterfront home with the city centre and surrounding communities.

Colin Chong, Everton’s Chief Real Estate and Regeneration Officer, said: “From the outset, our ambition for Hill Dickinson Stadium extended far beyond delivering a upcoming home for Everton Football Club. It was also about unlocking the potential of Liverpool’s northern waterfront and providing a catalyst for wider investment, regeneration and economic growth.

“We are already seeing the positive impact of the stadium on the surrounding area, with new businesses establishing themselves and existing businesses benefiting from increased footfall and activity.

“The updated Liverpool Waters masterplan provides an opportunity to build on that momentum. Upcoming public spaces, improved walking routes and better connectivity will complement our own investment in establishing Hill Dickinson Stadium and our Budweiser Plaza as a year-round destination, enhancing the appeal of the area, attracting more visitors and creating further opportunities for businesses, investment and employment across North Liverpool.”.

The growing programme of major sporting and entertainment events at Hill Dickinson Stadium is extending the economic benefits of Everton’s investment beyond football matchdays and across the wider Liverpool City Region.

As well as being the home for Everton's Premier League fixtures, Hill Dickinson Stadium has already hosted an international football fixture between Scotland and Côte d’Ivoire, a Rugby League Ashes Test, Magic WKND and a Rugby Union Nations Championship fixture, the stadium will also host matches during UEFA EURO 2028, with a programme of major concerts at the Club’s waterfront home set to get under way in summer 2027.

The ability to attract events of national and international significance is helping to further strengthen Liverpool’s reputation as a global sporting, cultural and entertainment destination, drawing additional visitors to the city, supporting its hotel, hospitality, retail and transport sectors, and creating further opportunities for investment and employment across the region.

Since the original Liverpool Waters masterplan was approved in 2013, the northern waterfront has undergone significant change, with the delivery of fresh residential developments, transport infrastructure, leisure and hospitality destinations and public spaces, alongside Hill Dickinson Stadium and the Isle of Man Ferry Terminal.

James Whittaker, Managing Director of Peel Waters, said: “The approval of the updated Liverpool Waters masterplan marks another major milestone in the transformation of Liverpool’s northern waterfront. Since the original masterplan was approved in 2013, we have delivered significant progress across the site, including newly introduced homes, public spaces, leisure destinations, major transport infrastructure and the new Everton Stadium, helping establish Liverpool Waters as one of the UK’s most ambitious regeneration projects.

“This updated framework reflects the considerable investment already made by Peel Waters and our partners, while providing the flexibility needed to respond to evolving market demand and future opportunities. With over £81 million of infrastructure investment committed at Central Docks, Princes Dock nearing completion and a clear vision for future neighbourhoods, Liverpool Waters is entering an exciting new chapter that will continue to create homes, jobs, investment and opportunities for Liverpool and the wider city region.”.

The revised framework also strengthens commitments around sustainability, biodiversity, climate resilience and the preservation of Liverpool’s rich maritime heritage – principles that were central to the development of Everton’s waterfront home.

Pete Swift, CEO and Co-Founder, Planit – the landscape architecture, urban design and masterplanning studio who also worked as part of the team to deliver Everton's new home, added: “We are overjoyed at the approval, not just for the Peel Waters and Liverpool Waters team but for the communities of Liverpool.

“A network of green and blue spaces, with the central park at the heart, now forms the backbone for our neighbourhoods. We understand better the assets that sit below the ground and the history on and above it – views old and new structure the place.

Sources indicate that “Hill Dickinson stadium changes the game; literally – for Everton Football Club and North Liverpool. It was never in the original masterplan [from 2013] and so we must adapt to respond to it and the opportunities it brings. Our wider variety of homes now represents a more inclusive, family-focused, inter-generational Liverpool Waters.

“Today’s consent embodies Peel Waters’ future-facing attitude and commitment to the quality of buildings and their supporting infrastructure – to remake a place that will play a major role in North Liverpool’s sustainable future.”.

The approved masterplan retains Liverpool Waters’ five-neighbourhood structure comprising Princes Dock, KINGS, Central Docks, Clarence Docks and Northern Docks.

Liverpool Waters also sits within the proposed Liverpool City Region Mayoral Development Zone, an initiative designed to accelerate regeneration, support investment and unlock the delivery of fresh homes, jobs and infrastructure.

The approval of Peel Waters' updated masterplan represents the next stage in the evolution of Liverpool’s northern waterfront, building on the investment made by Everton in delivering Hill Dickinson Stadium and the Club’s longstanding ambition for its new home to be a driver of economic growth, regeneration and lasting opportunities for North Liverpool and the wider city region.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European Union top officials and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced deals on trade and youth mobility at Friday's Brussels summit.

This might be the first step to rebuild ties, a decade after Britain voted to leave the EU.

During the delegations' meeting, Burnham stated the deal was a "landmark agreement," while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called it a "turning point" in relations.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"This is a good day for Britain. This is a good day for Europe," Burnham remarked.

Speaking at the joint press conference, European Council President Antonio Costa noted the bloc respected the British decision to leave the EU and would respect its choice to strengthen ties in the post-Brexit era.

He said jokingly that the EU and UK "may drive on the opposite sides of the road, but what matters is they are heading for the same direction.".

Burnham noted that the deals were made with young people in mind, adding: "This deal is for you. This deal really is about lifting your life chances.".

He went further and said "Brexit took opportunities from young people," and that they have to "open up new opportunities" for young people.

Von der Leyen stated the youth experience project would "open horizons and create friendships that will last a lifetime.".

She noted the trade agreement is a "two way street" and it means "more choice for the customers.".

Von der Leyen also mentioned the agreement on the carbon market, saying that it would cut emissions and generate investments in cleaner industries.

She also stated Britain will rejoin the Erasmus+ program, adding, "We miss them so much.".

Burnham said the agreements reached Friday, however, represent the most the UK could achieve at the moment, "What we are announcing today is probably ‌the limit of what we can achieve in this ‌Parliament, given what needs ‌to be done to implement it.".

In September, Burnham said he would seek a political consensus on the country's future relationship with the EU, even suggesting he could campaign to take Britain back into the bloc at the next election.

Sources indicate that "Britain and Europe share values, interests and a global neighborhood. In a more dangerous world, we are stronger together. A closer partnership with Europe is good for working people, good for Britain and good for Europe," Burnham said as he arrived in Brussels.

The three key agreements establish ways to:.

The "youth experience scheme" would allow 100,000 people under 30 from each side to reside for up to three years in each other's territory for work, study or travel without being subject to existing visa requirements.

Recent findings suggest that no deal was reached on tuition fees for EU students studying in Britain, a deal-breaker for the bloc. The EU has pressed for the UK to reduce university tuition fees for EU students to the same level paid by British students.

"There will be further discussions coming out of it on issues including on tuition fees," Burnham remarked.

Von der Leyen ‌said ⁠she was confident negotiators would reach a ​solution ​on ‌tuition fees, "We will be working ‌on that in ‌the ​next month and as we have a ​track record of finding ⁠solutions,.".

Recent findings suggest that on the food deal, the EU and UK have agreed to scrap certificates and border checks on food and animal products to ease post-Brexit trade. In return, Britain will align more closely with EU food safety and animal health rules.

They also agreed to link their emissions-trading systems, allowing them to recognize each other's carbon allowances and exempt traded goods from carbon border taxes.

According to the AFP news agency, London estimates the deal could boost the British economy by 3.8 billion pounds annually, and spare 6.5 billion pounds worth of steel, aluminum and other industrial exports from additional taxation.

Leaders said they will establish a "structured dialogue on migration." Their joint summit statement said this would include "engagement with third countries" and "returns to third countries," among other issues.

The two sides agreed to launch formal talks on economic security and strengthen cooperation on export controls and supply chains, among other areas.

On Monday, Burnham mentioned it ​was the "obvious truth" that ‌Britain had lost more than it had gained from Brexit.

Polling firm YouGov runs a regular tracker on whether the UK was right or wrong to vote to quit.

Since mid-2022, a majority of people surveyed stated Britain was wrong to leave.In September, the "Bregret" camp rose to 60% — the highest ever.

The Premier League is set to introduce a newly introduced LGBTQ+ inclusion campaign after ending its partnership with Stonewall, the charity behind the widely recognised Rainbow Laces initiative.

It has been revealed that stonewallâs Rainbow Laces campaign, introduced in 2013, became a fixture across English football, with players from all Premier League clubs wearing rainbow-coloured laces and captains donning rainbow armbands to promote acceptance and equality. The campaign aimed to support LGBTQ+ rights and foster inclusivity among fans and young people.

After over a decade of collaboration, the league will now lead its own campaign, timed to coincide with LGBTQ+ History Month in February, The Telegraph report.

"Rainbow Laces has benefited from a wide range of partners with a natural ebb and flow reflecting cultural and sporting changes," a Stonewall spokesperson told BBC Sport.

"Alongside other sporting bodies the FA has been instrumental in advancing LGBTQ+ inclusion at the grassroots level and more recently the Women's Super League has taken up the mantle as the women's game has grown - enabling Rainbow Laces to reach more diverse audiences.".

Despite Stonewall's efforts, recent reports from Kick It Out reveal an alarming increase in discriminatory incidents in football, including rises in sexism, transphobia and faith-based abuse, with racism continuing to be the most prevalent concern.

Controversies around playersâ attitudes to rainbow armbands have also made headlines. Last season, Ipswich captain Sam Morsy declined to wear one due to religious beliefs, while Crystal Palaceâs Marc GuÃ©hi faced criticism for personalising his armband with the phrase âI Love Jesus.â.

Additionally, Manchester United scrapped plans for LGBTQ+ support jackets after a player refused to participate.

With no openly gay or bisexual players currently in the Premier League, and the surge in discriminatory incidents, some question the timing of the split from Stonewall â an organisation highly respected for its work in LGBTQ+ advocacy.

Details of the Premier Leagueâs new campaign are still under wraps, but as the league presses âreset,â thereâs hope it will introduce a meaningful and effective initiative that advances equality rather than undermines it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that large regions of chromosomes are organized into a state known as heterochromatin. This densely packed form of DNA represses gene activity. Curiously, some families of clustered genes can be activated even though they are packed as heterochromatin. Writing in Nature, Buckley et al.1 report findings that explain this paradox: they show how opposing mechanisms that control the organization of heterochromatin promote the stochastic activation of genes in the protocadherin (Pcdh) gene cluster, thereby supporting proper nervous-system development.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, this Christmas, a lifelong Evertonian is sharing how Everton in the Community helped him survive the loneliest time of his life after his wife died just 12 hours after the birth of their second son. Sean Foster, from Wigan, lost his wife Taylor in the early hours of 1 July 2020. Taylor was just 25 years old and passed away due to a splenic artery aneurysm, after being found unresponsive by staff on the mother and baby ward. Sean faced the devastating reality of raising two young children without his wife, while navigating grief, anxiety and suicidal thoughts. He noted: “I’ve been through grief before, but this was something else. “You’re not just grieving for the person you’ve lost; it’s the future you had with them, it’s what they’ll miss out on with the kids and what the kids will miss out on with having their mum. “With grief also came overwhelming struggles with PTSD, depression, anxiety and suicidal ideation. One thing that accompanies grief, which I have found the hardest and most persistent to cope with, is loneliness.”Just six days after Taylor's death, Sean reached out to Everton in the Community on Twitter (now X) in the middle of the night – a decision he described as his “hail Mary” and the first step towards seeking help. “My newborn baby and his two-year-old brother were asleep, and I found myself feeling completely alone, drowning in grief and crying uncontrollably. “It was a hail Mary. I just needed to reach out to someone and, as an Evertonian, I knew about Everton in the Community – but I didn’t expect the level of help I did get. It was a lifesaver.”  A donation to Everton in the Community this Christmas will help the official charity of Everton Football Club to support more people like Sean and to ensure no one has to face loneliness alone. Although Sean had immense support from friends and family, he didn’t want to worry them. He continued: “By lunchtime, I had a response from Everton in the Community and just a couple of hours after that I was on the phone with them. “The support I got from them was second to none and I know I would have found that period of my life so much harder if I hadn’t reached out.”Donate to Everton in the CommunityA member of Everton in the Community’s team visited Sean, providing essential items to help him care for his two young sons. The charity's wellbeing team also signposted him to additional organisations for grief support, while regular phone calls gave Sean someone to turn to during some of his most difficult moments. He also received support in navigating practical challenges, including his finances and helping his children understand what had happened. Sean received a call from Everton legend Duncan Ferguson on the day Taylor's cause of death was confirmed. Taking the time to ask Sean about his wife and what she was like, the conversation marked an notable moment in his journey, helping him take the first steps towards talking about Taylor again. “Taylor was a force to be reckoned with,” Sean said. “She was genuinely one of a kind. A lot of people will say it about her, she was so thoughtful and she always looked out for others before herself. “Even the gifts she’d give on birthdays and Christmas, she’d know exactly what each person wanted and needed, make a care package, wrap it nicely and put a bow on it. “She was really into her arts and crafts and my eldest, he had two years with her, one of the things he always remembers is colouring with his mum.” Reflecting on the importance of having someone to turn to, Sean states he dreads to think about what might have happened had he not reached out to EitC. “I was in a really dark place and considering suicide," he admitted. "It’s not that I wanted to die. I wanted the kids to have a full family, a mum and dad figure and a safe, stable home. At that point in time I didn’t think I was giving them that. If I hadn’t reached out or got a response, I really struggle to think where I’d be.” Sean has since become an advocate for men’s mental health, including volunteering for Andy’s Man Club and starting his own podcast about grief. He has received therapy and attends group support sessions where he passionately talks about issues such as loneliness. He said: “The loneliest I have ever felt was at Christmas, the year Taylor died. All my family were crammed into my mum and dad's house, as we do every year, all 20-plus of us in the living room, scrambling to find our pile of presents as we did every year. “Only this year, Taylor wasn’t there laughing at the Christmas chaos. To this day I have never felt as lonely as I did in that moment.” Although he still experiences moments of loneliness, Sean says the support he has received has helped him understand that he doesn't have to face them alone. He hopes that by sharing his experience, he can encourage others who may be struggling to reach out, particularly during a time of year when feelings of loneliness can become more difficult. Sean said: “Loneliness isn’t the same as being alone. “We can have people around us, we can see friends, family, colleagues daily, but we can still feel lonely. “What I found about loneliness, particularly as a man, is that there's a stigma around talking about it, there's an expectation that we should just be strong, just get on with it and deal with it ourselves. “Most of the time that is the expectation we put on ourselves, when the fact is the real strength is in asking for help, admitting we might need a hand every now and then. “I still experience moments of loneliness, but they aren't as all-consuming. Thanks to Everton in the Community, I've learned I'm never truly alone.”  A donation to Everton in the Community this Christmas could help someone facing loneliness find the support they need – someone to listen and somewhere to turn when things feel impossible.

Taking the time to ask Sean about his wife and what she was like, the conversation marked an notable moment in his journey, helping him take the first steps towards talking about Taylor again.

“Taylor was a force to be reckoned with,” Sean mentioned. “She was genuinely one of a kind. A lot of people will say it about her, she was so thoughtful and she always looked out for others before herself.

“Even the gifts she’d give on birthdays and Christmas, she’d know exactly what each person wanted and needed, make a care package, wrap it nicely and put a bow on it.

“She was really into her arts and crafts and my eldest, he had two years with her, one of the things he always remembers is colouring with his mum.”.

Reflecting on the importance of having someone to turn to, Sean claims he dreads to think about what might have happened had he not reached out to EitC.

It has been revealed that “I was in a really dark place and considering suicide," he admitted. "It’s not that I wanted to die. I wanted the kids to have a full family, a mum and dad figure and a safe, stable home. At that point in time I didn’t think I was giving them that. If I hadn’t reached out or got a response, I really struggle to think where I’d be.”.

Sean has since become an advocate for men’s mental health, including volunteering for Andy’s Man Club and starting his own podcast about grief. He has received therapy and attends group support sessions where he passionately talks about complications such as loneliness.

According to recent reports, he said: “The loneliest I have ever felt was at Christmas, the year Taylor died. All my family were crammed into my mum and dad's house, as we do every year, all 20-plus of us in the living room, scrambling to find our pile of presents as we did every year.

“Only this year, Taylor wasn’t there laughing at the Christmas chaos. To this day I have never felt as lonely as I did in that moment.”.

Although he still experiences moments of loneliness, Sean states the support he has received has helped him understand that he doesn't have to face them alone.

He hopes that by sharing his experience, he can encourage others who may be struggling to reach out, particularly during a time of year when feelings of loneliness can become more difficult.

Sean said: “Loneliness isn’t the same as being alone.

“We can have people around us, we can see friends, family, colleagues daily, but we can still feel lonely.

“What I found about loneliness, particularly as a man, is that there's a stigma around talking about it, there's an expectation that we should just be strong, just get on with it and deal with it ourselves.

“Most of the time that is the expectation we put on ourselves, when the fact is the real strength is in asking for help, admitting we might need a hand every now and then.

Sources indicate that “I still experience moments of loneliness, but they aren't as all-consuming. Thanks to Everton in the Community, I've learned I'm never truly alone.”.

A donation to Everton in the Community this Christmas could help someone facing loneliness find the support they need – someone to listen and somewhere to turn when things feel impossible.

Published: 13:07 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 15:37 EST, 27 November 2026.

Ross Desmond started it at last season’s comedy turn of a Celtic AGM when more or less admitting that finances mean it’s time to run up the white flag when trying to compete in Europe.

And manager Martin O’Neill’s team selections in this term’s Europa League only heighten the concern that addressing a truly horrific record in UEFA competition dating back two decades now is not a priority.

Sources indicate that it is a desperate situation for the club to be in. O’Neill might talk about rotation or private masterplans over impact substitutions, but it is seriously wrong that Camilo Duran, for example, was left on the bench for the recent meetings with Besiktas and Torreense.

Duran, himself, proved it by coming on and scoring the goals that mean qualification for the knockout rounds remains a distinct possibility despite everything.

It just looks like the club and its manager don’t really care all that much about Europe – or don’t see it as a key priority – and that’s not acceptable when they have charged their punters massive-money for packages to get into the ground to watch it.

There are a number of things that need addressed when this year’s AGM rolls back around next Tuesday, though, and it is to be hoped punters and shareholders – probably the same thing, really – have prepared with cooler heads this time round.

Celtic line up for their tie against Torreense, with star man Camilo Duran again left on the bench.

Last year became embarrassing, really, with people holding up red cards, jeering, walking out and chanting ‘Sack The Board’. They gave those at the top table the opportunity to bring the meeting to a halt and that’s exactly what happened before they had been properly challenged.

Industry observers note that that behaviour is OK when making a point inside the stadium on matchday. If you want to win an argument – or unpick one – inside a business meeting, though, the shouting has to be replaced with clear thinking, planning and strong cases delivered in a coherent manner.

Sources indicate that there are so many things to tear into CEO Michael Nicholson and co over. There’s the evident lack of long-term planning that has a 74-year-old in O’Neill still in charge of running the team.

According to recent reports, there’s recruitment, in the week of a tie-up with little-known Pluto Data Analytics. Celtic went into their Champions League play-off with LASK Linz unprepared and suffered humiliation. Their dealings at the end of the summer window were erratic and scattergun.

Sources indicate that even marquee signings Kasper Hogh and Haissem Hassan are unravelling. They look like two guys totally unsuited to the way O’Neill wants to play and speak to a disjointed, failing policy.

There has been no full-time chairman appointed to replace 77-year-old interim Brian Wilson. There’s no sporting director or head of football operations. No one seems to want to explain who exactly will be working with Pluto to try and improve the club’s record on signings.

Martin O'Neill and assistant Shaun Maloney watch as Celtic toil against Torreense in Leiria.

Parkhead’s now old and outdated. Millions lie around in the bank for no particular reason. Communication between the board and a disgruntled fanbase needs improved dramatically.

In a recent development, there is a lot to get through next week. That’s why there can be no place for student politics, silly protests, angry chanting. This board needs taken to task and it is to be hoped there are fans ready to step up to the mic and confront them calmly.

Recent findings suggest that celtic regard themselves as one of the biggest clubs in the world. This apparent insouciance over Europe is at complete odds with that, though.

It is as clear a sign as any that standards have slipped so badly at the champions and it is something that needs to be called out and challenged in the right way.

According to recent reports, everton has confirmed a latest multi-year partnership with WTW, a leading global advisory, broking and solutions company, as the Club continues to expand its commercial portfolio into new categories. The agreement sees WTW become Everton’s ‘Official Insurance Partner’, bringing specialist expertise in insurance, risk management and analytics to support the Club’s operations and long-term ambitions. Operating across more than 140 countries and markets, WTW becomes the latest internationally-recognised business to join Everton’s growing partnership portfolio, following recent agreements with NOCO, Nestlé and JYSK. Through the agreement, WTW will benefit from brand visibility at Hill Dickinson Stadium and across Everton’s digital and social media channels as well as commercial activation opportunities through access to the Club’s waterfront home for client hospitality, business events and engagement activities. The agreement allows for wider collaboration, including community initiatives, that will also be explored. As Everton’s exclusive partner in the insurance brokerage category, WTW will also provide tailored risk and insurance advice and solutions, drawing on its global insurance-market relationships and extensive experience across the sports and entertainment industry. Mark Rollings, Chief Partnerships Officer at Everton, said: “We are delighted to welcome WTW as our Official Insurance Partner. “WTW is a highly respected global business with an outstanding reputation for expertise and innovation. This is a relationship that brings together two organisations with shared ambitions and a commitment to long-term success. “Alongside the international profile and opportunities Everton can offer WTW, the partnership will bring valuable specialist knowledge to the Club and create opportunities for collaboration beyond traditional sponsorship. “Welcoming another business of WTW’s calibre is a further demonstration of our commercial momentum and the growing appeal of Everton to leading international organisations.” WTW has an established presence across the global sports and entertainment sector, working with some the world’s best-known professional clubs, governing bodies, sporting events and venues to manage complex risks, strengthen resilience and support performance. Ian Tomlin, Global Sports and Entertainment Leader at WTW, said: “High-performing organisations, whether in sport or business, depend on resilience, specialist expertise and the confidence to make informed decisions. “Our partnership with Everton brings together the Club’s ambition and distinctive identity with WTW’s global insurance, risk and analytics expertise. “Together, we will help create greater resilience, improved risk management and performance, and lasting value on and off the pitch.”.
